### D-062 · 2026-11-13 · product-manager · US-008 delivery split (PR #20 code review M2, D-ORCH-022 (2)): TASK-010 delivers AT-US-008-01/02/04/05/06 and the api/worker log-line hops of AT-03; the audit hop is owned by TASK-029, the outbox hop by TASK-043, the job-payload hop by TASK-035, the Mock-carrier hop by TASK-079, and the end-to-end AT-US-008-03 assertion by TASK-092, which completes US-008; US-008 stays M0 Must, non-DC, nothing is split or deferred
- **Decision:** (1) US-008 is **not** completed by TASK-010. The plan sheets change from "TASK-010 completes US-008" to "TASK-010 partial; completed by TASK-092" (CLAUDE.md §7 step 3 form applied to task ownership only — the story's MoSCoW (Must), milestone (M0) and DC tag (none) are unchanged, as D-ORCH-022 (2) expected). (2) Scenario ownership. AT-US-008-01, -02, -04, -05, -06 → **TASK-010** (met in PR #20: validated/echoed/regenerated `X-Correlation-Id`, `request_id` + `client_correlation_id`, deep-walk redaction, e-mail masking, mandatory fields, body-free access lines). AT-US-008-03 ("One ID is visible end to end for the M0 booking") is decomposed by hop, following REQ-PLAT-011's own list (logs, audit entries, outbox events, queue jobs, outbound carrier calls): **api log lines and worker job log lines → TASK-010** (delivered: request context binds `correlation_id` to every api line including the error line; the worker job-context binds the payload's `correlation_id` to every job line); **audit entries → TASK-029** (the descriptor-driven middleware writes the request's correlation ID into every entry it creates — the entry *field* is TASK-025/US-087's, the *value carried from the request* is TASK-029's); **outbox event → TASK-043** (`outbox_events.correlation_id` is set from the request context of the business transaction by the writer, and the relay copies that value into the `correlation_id` of the payload v2 job it enqueues, so a correlation ID never changes between the row and the job); **job payload → TASK-035** (payload v2 `correlation_id` is populated by the producer from the originating request/outbox context — not generated — and the worker binds it as the logger's `correlation_id` for the whole job, re-proving TASK-010's binding on the real payload v2); **Mock carrier call → TASK-079** (every Mock adapter operation emits exactly one outbound carrier-call log line through TASK-010's `outboundCallFields` allow-list with `correlation_id` = `CarrierContext.correlationId` and no request/response body, and the call record it returns carries that correlation ID so the saga's `carrier_call` audit entry can cite it — this also lands the PR #20 code-review §5 note "carrier adapters must use `outboundCallFields`" on the first adapter); **end-to-end assertion → TASK-092** (one integration test titled with AT-US-008-03: POST the M0 booking with `X-Correlation-Id: demo-booking-0001`, run the saga through the worker on the Mock carrier, and assert that exactly that value appears in the api log lines, every audit entry of the booking (STATE_TRANSITION entries and the `carrier_call` entry), the outbox row, the BullMQ payload v2, the worker log lines and the Mock carrier call record). TASK-092 completes US-008; US-008 reads as Implemented only when TASK-010, TASK-029, TASK-035, TASK-043, TASK-079 and TASK-092 are all merged. **TASK-047 is not an owner** (it resolves tenant context from `platform.job_context`, not correlation; its `job-context.ts` edits must keep TASK-010's correlation binding, which TASK-035's line and TASK-092's end-to-end test catch). (3) Dependency order is already satisfied: TASK-092 depends on TASK-084 (→ TASK-029, TASK-043), TASK-043 (→ TASK-039 → TASK-035 → TASK-010) and TASK-079, so no `plan-data.mjs` dependency change is needed (contrast D-061, which added TASK-089 → TASK-014). Wave 2 is inside the generator's [0, 3] window for an M0 non-DC Must. (4) Traceability v1.6: REQ-PLAT-011 Task(s) = `TASK-010, TASK-029, TASK-035, TASK-043, TASK-079, TASK-092`, status "Planned (partial: TASK-010 validate/generate/echo + api/worker log lines; completes with TASK-029 (audit), TASK-043 (outbox → job), TASK-035 (payload v2 → worker logger), TASK-079 (Mock carrier call) and TASK-092 (end-to-end AT-US-008-03))"; REQ-PLAT-012 (Pino fields and redaction) stays wholly TASK-010. No REQ or story IDs, links, priorities, milestones or DC tags change; counts 434 / 91 / 293 / DC 134 unchanged. (5) Demo coverage confirmed: PRD §6.1 "One mock booking flows API → queue → worker (… correlation ID)" is demonstrated by TASK-092 (batch 2.5), which precedes TASK-121 M0 exit-demo journeys (batch 3.7, depends on TASK-094 → TASK-092). (6) PR #20 body and sheet: "partially completes US-008"; the AT-US-008-03 test in PR #20 keeps its title with a "(api and worker log lines; end to end in TASK-092)" suffix rather than being deleted. (7) STATUS: the fold is already queued under SHEET-FOLD-2 by D-ORCH-022; the exact sheet lines are in the D-062 handoff.
- **Why:** The logger is real (reviewer-verified: linear regexes, reserved keys, never-throw, identifier-only DB serializer), but four of the six hops in AT-03 describe data written by components that do not exist yet — the audit middleware, the outbox, payload v2 and the Mock adapter. Marking US-008 complete at TASK-010 would have let traceability show REQ-PLAT-011 Implemented while the propagation half of its text ("propagate it to … audit entries, outbox events, queue jobs and outbound carrier calls") had no owner — the silent drop PR #20 M2 flagged, identical to PR #13 M1. Ladder rung 4 (split into a smaller Must plus a Should) is wrong: nothing leaves R0 and every hop is still Must; only task ownership changes. Per-hop lines on the component owners rather than everything on TASK-092 because each component is the only place the value can be *set* correctly, and a saga-level test alone would surface a broken hop two waves after the component merged; the end-to-end assertion sits on TASK-092 because it is the first task where all six hops exist in one process chain (API → outbox → queue → worker → Mock carrier is its title). TASK-079 rather than TASK-092 for the Mock carrier hop because the adapter is the only code that can emit the outbound line with the context's ID, and it is the first `CarrierAdapter` implementation, so the `outboundCallFields` rule from PR #20 §5 must be proven there before the real DHL/FedEx/UPS adapters copy it. TASK-035 rather than TASK-043 for the payload-to-logger binding because payload v2 and the worker queue platform are TASK-035's artefacts; TASK-043 owns only the copy from the row into the payload it enqueues.
- **Alternatives:** Keep "TASK-010 completes US-008" and rely on the PR body (rejected: traceability and G3 read the sheets, not PR bodies). Put the whole of AT-03 on TASK-092 only (rejected: no hop would be proven at the component that sets it; a defect would surface in wave 2 instead of the owning wave). Create a new "correlation end-to-end" enabler task (rejected: dispatch-state churn, and TASK-092 already runs exactly that chain for US-202; D-ARCH-079 set the precedent of no new `late` task). Ladder rung 4 — split US-008 into a Must plus a Should (rejected: no scope is leaving R0; a Should would wrongly signal that end-to-end tracing may slip). Assign the Mock-carrier hop to TASK-047 as the PR suggested (rejected: TASK-047 is tenant context; it never touches the carrier adapter).
- **Reversibility:** High (sheet lines, a story note, one traceability row; `plan-data.mjs` folded by the architect batch under SHEET-FOLD-2).

### D-063 · 2026-11-13 · product-manager · AT-US-007-02 wording aligned with OPTIONS/405 `Allow` parity (PR #21 / TASK-017 code review R1-m3, D-ORCH-023 (2)): a 405 `Allow` lists every method the route supports including OPTIONS, and OPTIONS on a known route is 204 with the same `Allow`; US-007 stays M0 Must, non-DC; no scope change
- **Decision:** (1) AT-US-007-02 ("405 includes the Allow header", `docs/01-requirements/stories/EPIC-01-platform-foundation.md`) now reads: When DELETE is sent to a route that supports only GET and HEAD, Then `Allow` is "GET, HEAD, OPTIONS", And OPTIONS sent to the same route returns 204 with no body and the same `Allow` header. The former text ("GET, HEAD") contradicted the reviewed and implemented R1-m3 fix (`apps/api/src/platform/http/fallback.ts`, `tests/api/helpers/contract-validator.ts`, `tests/contract-stubs/stubs.ts`). The scenario title is unchanged so `docs/05-quality/tests/gherkin-test-map.md` row AT-US-007-02 (`api`, B) remains valid without edit; no other US-007 scenario changes. (2) REQ-PLAT-010 (REQUIREMENTS.md → 1.8) note: "The 405 response carries an `Allow` header listing every method the route supports, including OPTIONS (RFC 9110 §15.5.6); OPTIONS on a known route is 204 with the same `Allow`." The "shall" sentence, ID, M0, Must are unchanged. (3) US-007 notes record the amendment and point to this decision. (4) PRD → 1.8 (§11 row); NFR.md (1.5) and `traceability.md` (1.6) untouched: no ID, link, priority, milestone, DC tag or count changes (434 / 91 / 293 / DC 134), and REQ-PLAT-010's traceability row (TASK-006, Implemented) is a task-ownership fact this wording does not alter — the parity behaviour was delivered by TASK-017 on top of TASK-006's handler and is verified by PR #21's own tests; qa-lead's Test(s) column picks it up at the usual time. (5) Not done here: `docs/03-architecture/api/README.md` §3 "OPTIONS 204 + `Allow` including OPTIONS / 405 `Allow` lists OPTIONS" line — api-designer owns it per D-ORCH-023 (1); no code is touched.
- **Why:** RFC 9110 §15.5.6 requires a 405 to carry an `Allow` field listing the target resource's currently supported methods, and §9.3.7 makes OPTIONS a method the resource supports whenever it answers OPTIONS — which every known route now does (204). An acceptance test that pins "GET, HEAD" would therefore fail a correct server and pass one that violates the RFC, and would force the reviewers to choose between the story text and the standard at every future 405 test. The AC is the only place the exact list is written down; REQ-PLAT-010 only said "carries an `Allow` header", so the note is sharpened to carry the rule (list every supported method, OPTIONS included) rather than a literal header value, keeping the requirement atomic and testable on any route. The parity "And" line is added inside AT-US-007-02 rather than as a new scenario because R1-m3's finding was precisely that three components disagreed on one behaviour; a 405-only assertion would not catch the 204/405 drifting apart again, and adding a scenario would be a backlog change the task did not ask for. Nothing moves in or out of R0; US-007 is Must, non-DC, so no demo path is affected. Classified as a wording amendment (D-059/D-060 convention: PRD §11 row, REQUIREMENTS.md version bump, story note; traceability untouched), not a delivery split (D-061/D-062) and not a re-scope.
- **Alternatives:** Leave the AC at "GET, HEAD" and revert R1-m3 (rejected by D-ORCH-023 and here: contradicts RFC 9110 and the reviewed code). Change only the literal in the Then line without touching REQ-PLAT-010 (rejected: the REQ would stay silent on what `Allow` must contain, so the next reader could again infer "GET, HEAD" from Express defaults; one note clause removes the ambiguity at no cost). Make the OPTIONS 204 behaviour a new REQ/story (rejected: it is framework behaviour inside REQ-PLAT-010's "unsupported method" mapping and api/README §3's domain; a new ID for a header-parity rule is churn with no product value). Write the Then line as a regex/"contains OPTIONS" (rejected: a fixed, ordered list on a known fixture route is the more deterministic test; the REQ note carries the general rule).
- **Reversibility:** High (one AC line and one "And" line, one REQ note clause, two version rows; no code, IDs, priorities or counts).

### D-ARCH-080 · 2026-11-13 · principal-architect · PR19-SEC-01 (INFO) SYSTEM-model access control: SYSTEM-class delegates leave the top-level `TenantDb` and are reached only through `systemDelegates(tx)`, whose importers a manifest-driven lint rule restricts to the owning module; mechanism on TASK-020, first consumer TASK-040 (`idempotency_keys`), then TASK-043/047/052
- **Decision:** (1) Data-model §1.5 "SYSTEM tables: only the owning module's repositories" gets a mechanical control (PR #19 security review options 2 + 1 combined): SYSTEM-class models — the class comes from the table-class manifests — are **excluded from the top-level `TenantDb` delegate set** at type level (the `TenantDb` type omits them) and at run time (the guarded proxy throws `TenantDbAccessError` naming the port), and are reachable only through `systemDelegates(tx)` exported from `apps/api/src/platform/db/system-db.ts` (worker twin under `apps/worker/src/platform/db/`). (2) A manifest-driven ESLint rule `platform/system-model-owner` restricts the importers of that accessor, per model, to the module whose manifest declares the table: `platform/outbox` for `outbox_events`, `platform/idempotency` for `idempotency_keys`, `modules/identity` for `login_attempt_counters`, the worker platform for `job_context` and `processed_events`, the payments webhook module for `gateway_webhook_events`; one negative fixture (a module repository touching the outbox delegate outside the allow-list fails lint) and a `prisma/tests/rls` test (the `referenceDatasetVersion` delegate is absent from `TenantDb` while `systemDelegates(tx)` reaches it inside the same transaction). GLOBAL catalogue delegates stay in `TenantDb` (read-only by grant). (3) Owner of the mechanism: **TASK-020** (holds the `lint` lock and wires the `tx` slot, the only `TenantDb` hand-out point; batch 0.6, before every SYSTEM writer). Consumers: TASK-040 `idempotency_keys` (batch 1.2 — the first writable, sensitive SYSTEM model, earlier than the review's TASK-043 guess), TASK-043 `outbox_events`, TASK-047 `job_context`/`processed_events`, TASK-052 `login_attempt_counters`; later SYSTEM models are covered by the generic rule. (4) data-model §1.5 row amended, §12 A21.
- **Why:** The boundaries plugin sees imports, not property access, and grants are per role, not per module; once `outbox_events` and `idempotency_keys` carry `platform_app` write (and hard-delete) grants, "only the owning module" is a real control with nothing enforcing it. Removing the delegates from `TenantDb` makes the wrong access a compile error and a runtime throw; the lint rule guards the one escape hatch with a fixture. Owner TASK-020 rather than the first consumer because the consumer tasks do not hold the lint lock and the mechanism must exist before the first writer merges.
- **Alternatives:** Lint-only rule on `db.<model>` member access (rejected alone: aliasing `const d = db` defeats a syntactic rule; kept as the guard on the accessor). Per-call-site `TenantDb` views with an explicit model allow-list (rejected: a per-caller discipline with no fixture and no single hand-out point). Do nothing until a sensitive model lands (rejected: TASK-040 lands in batch 1.2 and the review asked for the choice before it).
- **Reversibility:** Medium (a type and proxy filter plus one lint rule; removing it later is a one-line change, adding it after writers exist is a sweep).

### D-ARCH-081 · 2026-11-13 · principal-architect · Ratification of D-TASK021-01 (1) / PR #24: readiness `audit_partitions` is critical with three states (`unavailable` for a missing required month or a squat, `degraded` only when month current+3 is missing, else `ok`); AT-US-012-04 "the next audit partition" = month current+3; `HealthReady` enum gains `unavailable` in PR #24; union checklist
- **Decision:** (1) Ratified as implemented in PR #24: the `audit_partitions` readiness component is **critical**; `unavailable` (HTTP 503) when any month in [current, current+2] lacks a verified attached partition or any object squats a partition name (data-model §5.3 item 3, D-ARCH-076); `degraded` (HTTP 200) only when every required month is present but month current+3 — the one the daily `audit-maintenance` job creates ahead of the required window — is missing; `ok` otherwise. (2) AT-US-012-04 ("Given the next audit partition is missing … 200 and component audit is degraded") is satisfied without a wording change: "the next audit partition" is month current+3; the TASK-033 fixture drops exactly that month (200 degraded) and a month at +1/+2 (503 unavailable). (3) `HealthReady.components.audit_partitions` enum = `ok | degraded | unavailable` (openapi.yaml) lands **in PR #24** — api-designer did not touch it on `main`; `audit_chain` stays non-critical (`ok | degraded`). (4) PR #24 must merge `main` (PR #21 pipeline) and in that union: regenerate `packages/shared/src/api/types.gen.ts` (the enum change alters the generated types; the lane A types-drift test would otherwise fail); route `audit_partition_squatted` and `audit_mutation_rejected` through the PR #20 security sink as `RUNTIME_SECURITY_EVENTS` at `error` (not a raw `log.warn('security.…')`, which PR #20 treats as an ordinary line) with the per-event field allow-list of api/README §13 runtime table (`partition_name, kind, reason, sql_state` and `sql_state`), relaxing PR #20's `['sql_state']`-only expectation for runtime events to a per-event expectation; carry the traceability extensions. (5) data-model §5.3 item 3 amended; TASK-021 sheet carries a post-merge note only (PR #24 is not reopened).
- **Why:** A missing required month means the next audit write may fail (`audit_write_failed`, 500) — that is an outage signal, so 503 is right; a missing +3 month is a maintenance-job lag with two months of headroom, so 200 degraded is right and keeps the story's intent (readiness does not fail on audit housekeeping). Reading "next" as current+1 would make the story contradict D-ARCH-076's contiguity rule; reading it as current+3 keeps both.
- **Alternatives:** Keep `audit_partitions` non-critical with two states (rejected: a squat or a missing current month would leave the API "ready" while audit writes fail); amend AT-US-012-04 to say "+3" (rejected: no behaviour change, and the AC title is referenced by the gherkin test map — the fixture definition on TASK-033 is enough).
- **Reversibility:** High (threshold constants and an enum value).

### D-ARCH-082 · 2026-11-13 · principal-architect · Ratification of D-TASK011-01 / PR #23: evidence schema at `tools/quality/summary.schema.json` (ADR-0023 am. B path withdrawn, am. K item 2); suite-activation protocol = manifest-only PRs by qa-lead at four checkpoints (W0-ACT-1, Wave-0 exit, v0.1.0-m0, G3) while the checker keeps reading the base manifest
- **Decision:** (1) The `summary.json` schema lives at **`tools/quality/summary.schema.json`** (the sheet path), not `docs/05-quality/tests/schema/heavy-run.schema.json`: it is a tooling input of a security-critical checker (`tools/quality/**` is in `security_critical_paths`, SEC-P3-31) and must be code-owned and versioned with `check-evidence.mjs`. ADR-0023 am. B line struck with a dated note; am. K item 2. qa-lead updates `tooling_inputs` (both `tools/quality/required-suites.json` and the schema) and TEST-STRATEGY §9.1. (2) **Activation protocol.** `quality:check-evidence` keeps reading the **base-ref** manifest and requires only `active` suites; `quality:heavy` runs only `active` suites (`planned` suites are listed in `summary.md`, never as JUnit — PR #23 already behaves so; rule 4 of TEST-STRATEGY §9.2 stands). Activation is a **manifest-only PR by qa-lead** (security-analyst review per §9.3) that lands after a suite's first tests merge and before the next evidence-carrying PR, batched at four checkpoints: **W0-ACT-1** — immediately after PR #23 merges, every suite whose tests exist on `main` (at least `unit`, `integration`, `migrations`, `catalog-c1-c14`, `migration-lint`, `config-guards`, `sec-static`, `ci-policy`, `lint`, `typecheck`, `contract-openapi`, `e2e-chromium`, `e2e-webkit`; `redaction` once PR #20 is in); **Wave-0 exit** — every T-QA-04 generator and security suite (`rbac-matrix`, `audit-generator`, `audit-immutability`, `rls-cross-tenant`, `abuse`, `route-registry`) plus `compose-up`, `image-assertions`; **v0.1.0-m0 tag** — every suite whose owning task has merged; **G3** — everything `active` or in `deferred_at_gate` with a decision ID (§9.2 rule 5). `e2e-firefox` stays `planned` until COND-E2E-FF (lane B runs on the Windows host, D-ORCH-019). The orchestrator's wave-exit checklist records each checkpoint; the plan generator cannot verify it. (3) Owner: **qa-lead** (manifest content, §9.3); TASK-011 sheet carries a post-merge note only. (4) ADR-0023 am. K item 3 records the protocol.
- **Why:** The checker reading the base manifest is the SEC-P3-31 property (a PR cannot weaken or widen its own gate). Letting a PR activate a suite for itself would need a monotonicity carve-out in a security-critical tool and a security round; a manifest-only PR per checkpoint costs a docs-sized PR and keeps the property exact. Batching at checkpoints avoids one PR per suite while guaranteeing the Wave-0 exit and release states T-QA-04 and §9.2 rule 5 demand.
- **Alternatives:** Head-manifest activation with a planned-to-active-only diff rule (rejected: checker change on a security-critical path for a convenience); activate in the first-test PR (rejected: the base manifest does not see it, and an `active` suite with no JUnit yet fails every other PR's evidence); keep the schema under `docs/` (rejected: hand-editable without a security record).
- **Reversibility:** High (a path and a process rule).

### D-ARCH-083 · 2026-11-13 · principal-architect · PR21-SEC-03 / PR #21 N7 (b): the `DOCS_ENABLED` config default stands (on in local and test; staging and production opt in) and the requirement text follows it — product-manager aligns REQ-API-003 and the US-035 notes, api/README §1 done; a production opt-in carries the PR21-SEC-02 conditions
- **Decision:** (1) The configuration default `localOnly` (Swagger UI on by default only with `APP_ENV` local or test; staging and production need `DOCS_ENABLED=true`) is the design; REQ-API-003 ("on in local, test and staging") and the US-035 notes are aligned to it by product-manager as a wording amendment (D-059/D-060 convention; no ID, priority, milestone or count change). api/README §1 "Outside the prefix" row already reads so (api-designer, this fold). (2) A production opt-in is allowed by REQ-API-003 and carries the PR21-SEC-02 conditions — cookieless docs origin, try-it-out off (`supportedSubmitMethods: []`), `validatorUrl: null` — recorded in COND-G4-PROD by the orchestrator. (3) No TASK-014 change: there is no staging target this run (DEPLOY_TARGET_STAGING blank), so "set staging in env" has nothing to set.
- **Why:** The safer default matches TEST-STRATEGY D-QA-009 / SEC-TC-34 ("developer tools absent from non-local profiles") and the ASVS 14.2.2 reading the P3 review applied; a staging environment, when it exists, opts in explicitly in its environment, which is also where the cookieless-origin condition is checked.
- **Alternatives:** Change the default to include staging (rejected: widens the attack surface of every future staging by default and contradicts SEC-TC-34); leave the texts contradicting the code (rejected: the next reader infers the wrong default).
- **Reversibility:** High (one requirement note, one story note, one README row).

### D-ARCH-085 · 2026-11-13 · principal-architect · SPK-04 FALLBACK (TASK-018, PR #27 @aa1cfb1; D-ORCH-031): ADR-0007 amendment 10 — audit write path = batched vault + head-row `FOR UPDATE` lock with ≤ 2 round trips from lock grant to COMMIT, short audit `lock_timeout` → 503 `AUDIT_LOCK_TIMEOUT`, hot-tenant sub-streams deferred with a trigger, clean 300 rps re-measure on a quiet/Linux host (TASK-280); writer SQL rules; data-model §5.4 rewritten (`rulings/wave-0-spk04-rulings.md`)
- **Decision:** (1) TASK-030 builds the FALLBACK: per entry one multi-row `INSERT INTO audit_pii_vault … SELECT FROM unnest($arrays) ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING` and one separate lateral token lookup **before** the lock; **lever (a) adopted** — the stream lock is `SELECT entry_count, head_hash, head_occurred_at, clock_timestamp() FROM audit_stream_heads WHERE stream_id = $1 FOR UPDATE` (lock + head + clock in one round trip; the advisory lock is retired, OI-21 closed; a missing head is created once per stream with `INSERT … ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING` and re-locked); hash in-process; one CTE `WITH appended AS (INSERT INTO audit_entries …) UPDATE audit_stream_heads … WHERE stream_id = $1 AND entry_count = $seq − 1` with `expectAffected(1)`; COMMIT. **Design rule: at most two round trips from lock grant to COMMIT inclusive; nothing else under the lock; no lock after the head lock.** Round trips create (3 PII) 8, update 9, fail-closed VIEW 9, SYSTEM 6 (as written 15/12/12/9). (2) **Lever (c) adopted:** `DB_AUDIT_LOCK_TIMEOUT_MS` (default 250 ms, validated < `DB_TX_LOCK_TIMEOUT_MS`) applied by a `MATERIALIZED set_config('lock_timeout', $2, true)` CTE inside the lock statement (TASK-030 proves the bound with a held-row test; fallback a separate `SET LOCAL` round trip); 55P03 → 503 `AUDIT_LOCK_TIMEOUT` (retryable, `Retry-After: 1`, metric `audit_lock_timeout_total{stream_kind}`), distinct from 500 `AUDIT_WRITE_FAILED` (non-retryable); both roll back the business transaction (REQ-AUDIT-004, O4). (3) **Lever (b) hot-tenant sub-streams deferred**; trigger = the clean 300 rps run still shows hot-stream lock-wait p95 > 5 ms or Δp95 over budget with the 20 % hot share; design sketch recorded in am. 10 item 4; adoption needs a superseding amendment. (4) **Lever (d) adopted:** TASK-280 runs the clean 300 rps `audit-ab` on a quiet or native-Linux Docker host before G3 (D-ORCH-031 (2)); exit = budget met, hot-stream lock-wait p95 ≤ 5 ms, zero pool-exhaustion errors. (5) **Writer SQL rules** (TASK-030, data-model §5.4 (a)–(f), §8.3): multi-argument `unnest` and `extract(… FROM …)` stay unqualified (the two recorded grammar-level exceptions; 42883 / syntax error otherwise); no `RETURNING` on the CTE insert; typed array binds (`TenantDb` refuses `Prisma.join`/`Prisma.sql`); the token lookup is `unnest … WITH ORDINALITY CROSS JOIN LATERAL (… LIMIT 1)` or any shape whose `EXPLAIN` against ≥ 100 k vault rows is an index lookup per key (asserted in an integration test, exit E4); zero hash never a text expression. (6) TASK-030 exits E1 (statement-sequence test with a query spy), E2 (held-row fail-fast), E3 (REQ-AUDIT-012), E4 (plan); informational micro-benchmark in the PR report; title changed to "head-row lock". (7) TASK-029 line: one writer call per entry with the complete PII set, as the last database work; 503 + `Retry-After`, never 500, for lock/admission failures.
- **Why:** The spike measured lock-hold time = round trips under the lock × RTT (5 × 1.1–1.7 ms as written) and showed a 60 writes/s stream queueing (wait p95 229–603 ms) with waiters draining the pool for every tenant; the batched variant (3 round trips) still missed the budget on the saturated host. A round-trip count is a host-independent, lint-able design budget; `FOR UPDATE` under `READ COMMITTED` returns the latest committed head after waiting, so it is both the lock and the read. Sub-streams change chain semantics for a need that disappears once the hold time is 2 round trips on Linux-class RTT (utilisation ≈ 0.02 at 60 writes/s). A short lock wait keeps a hot tenant's failure on its own stream and retryable, instead of a platform-wide 503 at the pool.
- **Alternatives:** keep the advisory lock and only batch (rejected: 3 round trips under the lock and the `hashtext` collision caveat; measured insufficient); `INSERT … ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE … RETURNING` as the lock (rejected: writes a second tuple version per entry on the hot row); sub-streams now (rejected: ADR-0007 core change without a Linux-host measurement); `SET LOCAL` as a separate statement (fallback only; costs a round trip outside the lock); `pg_try_advisory_xact_lock` polling (rejected: more round trips).
- **Reversibility:** Medium — the lock form and the error code are internal to `packages/audit`; the chain definition and hash inputs are unchanged.

### D-ARCH-086 · 2026-11-13 · principal-architect · SPK-04 §5 finding 3 pool coupling: per-tenant admission bulkhead inside `withTenantTx` (TASK-025; worker twin TASK-047; data-model §7.7; ADR-0007 am. 10 item 3)
- **Decision:** `withTenantTx` admits, **before pool checkout**, at most `DB_TENANT_MAX_CONCURRENT_TX` concurrent transactions per admission key per process (default `max(2, floor(DB_POOL_MAX / 2))`; key = `ctx.orgId`, `anonymous` for `''`, `operator` for OPERATOR scope), FIFO wait ≤ `DB_TENANT_ADMISSION_WAIT_MS` (default 250 ms, ≤ `maxWait`), queue depth 2 × cap; overflow or wait expiry → `DbError` 503 `SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE` reason `TENANT_CONCURRENCY_LIMIT` (retryable, `Retry-After: 1`); metrics `db_tenant_admission_rejected_total{reason=wait|depth}`, `db_tenant_admission_inflight{key_kind}`; permit released in `finally`. Owner TASK-025 (`apps/api/src/platform/db/tenant-admission.ts` + wiring in `with-tenant-tx.ts`; config keys in `packages/config` without taking the `pkg-config` lock, D-ORCH-020 precedent); TASK-033 adds the two-tenant scenario; TASK-047 applies the worker twin.
- **Why:** A lock waiter holds its pool connection, so one hot stream exhausted the 10-connection pool and failed every tenant with `SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE` — a noisy-neighbour availability failure. The cap bounds a tenant's share of the pool to one half; D-ARCH-085 (2) bounds how long it holds that share. A `lock_timeout` alone does not bound the number of connections a hot tenant occupies (60 rps × 250 ms ≈ 15), and a separate audit pool cannot help because the audit write must share the business transaction.
- **Alternatives:** separate pool/semaphore inside the audit writer (rejected: the connection is already held from BEGIN; waiting inside the transaction changes nothing); per-IP/route rate limits only (rejected: a legitimate hot tenant is not abuse); a fair-share scheduler (rejected: complexity; two simultaneously hot tenants filling a pool is accepted for this run).
- **Reversibility:** High (a wrapper and three configuration keys).

### D-ARCH-087 · 2026-11-13 · principal-architect · SPK-04 §5 finding 5: data-model §5.4 step 3 zero-hash expression was `text` (42804 against `bytea`) — corrected to `decode(repeat('00', 32), 'hex')`; PR #24 (TASK-021) bootstrap verified clean
- **Decision:** §5.4 statement 2b now uses `decode(repeat('00', 32), 'hex')` (or a 32-zero-byte bind parameter); the rule "the zero hash is never a text expression" is on the TASK-025 and TASK-030 sheets. **PR #24 checked** (`git show origin/feat/TASK-021-audit-store-sql-partitioned-audit:prisma/bootstrap/10-audit.sql`): the `head_hash` and `last_verified_hash` `DEFAULT`s already read `decode(repeat('00', 32), 'hex')` and the branch's tests use `pg_catalog.decode(pg_catalog.repeat('00', 32), 'hex')` — the defect lives only in the data-model text; D-ORCH-031 (3)'s round-2 check can be closed as clean, no PR branch edit needed.
- **Why:** `'\x' || repeat('00', 32)` concatenates two `text` values; only the literal `'\x00…'` (or `::bytea`) is a bytea. The spike hit the 42804 in its first run.
- **Alternatives:** `'\x0000…00'::bytea` literal (equivalent; `decode` is clearer about the length).
- **Reversibility:** High (text).

### D-ARCH-088 · 2026-11-13 · principal-architect with product-manager · NFR-AUDIT-005 / NFR-PERF-001 measurement method wording and the A-029 re-baseline after SPK-04 (NFR.md v1.6, ASSUMPTIONS.md A-029/A-036; ADR-0007 am. 10 item 6; TEST-STRATEGY §7.10 `audit-ab` row routed to qa-lead)
- **Decision:** (1) NFR-AUDIT-005 method (product-manager applied, wording amendment under D-059/D-060; target unchanged): k6 `audit-ab` with the NFR-PERF-001 mix and a **20 % hot-tenant share** on one organisation stream, the fail-closed VIEW second transaction inside the route latency, audit on vs the **build-time `-bench` image** (never a runtime flag), ≥ 2 repetitions per rate with randomised arm order, **delta per repetition**, §7.10 validity per repetition, **pass = mean of valid per-repetition deltas within budget and no valid repetition over twice the budget**, measured at the maximum cleanly sustained rate; G3 column "FULL conditional on the TASK-280 valid 300 req/s run; otherwise PARTIAL with the sustained rate recorded". (2) NFR-PERF-001 method names audit-on + the hot share and the §7.10 INCONCLUSIVE clause (> 85 % CPU in more than 10 % of samples). (3) A-029 re-baselined: the shared Windows 11 / Docker Desktop host (i9-11950H, 16 logical CPUs, 32 GB) sustains the full mix with audit on at 150 req/s cleanly, not 300; a clean 300 req/s A/B needs a quiet or native-Linux Docker host (TASK-280 before G3); A-036 validation text aligned. Counts unchanged (91 NFRs, 75/10/6). (4) Routed to qa-lead: TEST-STRATEGY §7.10 `audit-ab` row ("`APP_ENV=benchmark` build" → build-time `-bench` image; add hot share, repetitions, per-repetition rule) and the `steady` row's A-029 note.
- **Why:** The spike showed that pooled means hide a failing repetition (150 rps rep 1 +22.1 ms vs rep 2 −2.3 ms) and that the hot share dominates the result; without it the budget is far easier and does not test R-ARCH-04. Per-repetition deltas with randomised arm order remove the "batched is always the last arm" bias the spike recorded.
- **Alternatives:** per-repetition pass only (rejected: one noisy repetition on a shared host would fail a sound design — the §7.10 validity rule already removes saturated runs, and the 2× guard catches a systematic miss); flip NFR-AUDIT-005 to PARTIAL now (rejected by product-manager: changes status counts before TASK-280 reports).
- **Reversibility:** High (wording).

### D-QA-014 · 2026-11-13 · qa-lead · W0-ACT-1 suite activation: `unit`, `integration`, `api`, `catalog-c1-c14`, `migrations` go `active`; SEC-TC IDs without a test on `main` are parked in `required_cases_pending`; active-needs-runner test; the 9 runner-less W0-ACT-1 candidates move to the Wave-0-exit activation
- **Decision:** (1) In the manifest-only W0-ACT-1 PR (D-ARCH-082 (2), D-ORCH-030, COND-PR23-2), `tools/quality/required-suites.json` marks `active` exactly the five suites that have a `tools/quality/suite-runners.json` entry and tests on `main`: `unit`, `integration`, `api` (due by the Wave-0 exit, D-ORCH-030; activated now), `catalog-c1-c14`, `migrations`. (2) `tools/quality/activation.test.ts` asserts that every `active` suite has a runner entry (plus a mutation case, no orphan runner entries, and the `required_cases_pending` invariants). (3) **Required cases.** Four SEC-TC IDs listed for these suites have no test on `main` (verified by name search): `unit` SEC-TC-14 and SEC-TC-55 (identity, TASK-049 / TASK-057), `integration` SEC-TC-22 (tracking, TASK-172, Wave 6), `api` SEC-TC-29 (shared API helper, TASK-020 with the first authenticated route). Left in `required_cases`, every lane-B PR would FAIL on `unit` from the next PR on. They move to a new informational manifest key `required_cases_pending` (suite, owner task, latest checkpoint: v0.1.0-m0, or G3 for SEC-TC-22) and return to `required_cases` at the first activation checkpoint after the owning task merges. `catalog-c1-c14` keeps SEC-TC-05 (two passing C4/C11 tests). The hard rule (a skipped or failed SEC-TC test case fails in any suite) is unchanged. (4) Deferred with checkpoint: `migration-lint`, `config-guards`, `sec-static`, `ci-policy`, `lint`, `typecheck`, `contract-openapi`, `e2e-chromium`, `e2e-webkit` → Wave-0 exit together with their runner entries (devops-engineer); `redaction` → Wave-0 exit once PR #20 is merged; `e2e-firefox` → held until COND-E2E-FF; every other suite → v0.1.0-m0 when its owning task has merged, else G3. TEST-STRATEGY §9.1–§9.3 (v1.1) and `docs/05-quality/README.md` (code review PR #23 R2-n1; new "Suite activation" section) aligned.
- **Why:** An `active` suite without a runner, or with a required case no test carries, fails closed on every PR that selects it, which would turn the first Wave-1 PRs into fix cycles for test IDs owned by later tasks. Parking the IDs with an owner and a due checkpoint keeps the intent auditable while enforcement starts now on the 2,500+ unit and 185+ integration tests that exist.
- **Alternatives:** Keep the IDs in `required_cases` and delay activation until the owning tasks land (rejected: prolongs the MEDIUM gap PR23-SEC-02 to Wave 6 for `integration`); delete the IDs from the manifest (rejected: loses the tracking); add runner entries for the nine runner-less suites in this PR (rejected by D-ORCH-030 "keep it minimal": they need `kind: command` runners and JUnit converters for non-Jest tools, devops-owned work for the Wave-0-exit PR).
- **Reversibility:** High (manifest status values and one informational key).

### D-ARCH-091 · 2026-11-13 · principal-architect · PR26-SEC-03 (LOW, PR #26 security r1): the stamped standard columns are enforced by the database as well — assertion-only guard trigger `platform.std_columns_guard()` on every runtime-writable STD table (catalog C15); no raw-DML lint; owners TASK-024 (mechanism) and TASK-037 (first application), due before TASK-037 merges
- **Decision:** (1) Option 1 of the security record is adopted **alone**: a database guard from the policy-template family. `platform.std_columns_guard()` is plpgsql, SECURITY INVOKER, `SET search_path = pg_catalog, pg_temp`, owned by `platform_migrator`, and reads the actor only through `platform.app_actor_id()`. One `BEFORE INSERT OR UPDATE FOR EACH ROW` trigger `trg_<table>__std_columns` is rendered from the table-class manifest for every table that carries the full STD set, is not `runtimeReadOnly` and is not owned by `platform_audit_owner`. It **asserts, never assigns**: INSERT requires `created_by = updated_by =` the actor (the reserved ANONYMOUS id when the context has none) and `version = 1`; UPDATE requires `id`, `created_at`, `created_by` unchanged, `updated_by =` the actor and `version = OLD.version + 1`; a violation raises `P0001` `STD_COLUMNS_VIOLATION: <column> on <schema>.<table> (<op>)` (no value; `mapDbError` default `DB_ERROR` 500; no new security event now, because the event catalogue and api/README §13 change together in code, PR #20 SEC-TC-63). `platform_migrator` is exempt (migration lane, reference seed). Timestamps are not constrained. (2) **No raw-DML lint is built**: the lint half of the security record (a `db-raw-sql` manifest of reviewed raw writers) is rejected, so TASK-024 takes no ESLint lock for it. (3) **Owners and deadline.** TASK-024 ships `prisma/sql/function-templates/std-columns-guard.sql`, the manifest-driven trigger rendering and catalog **C15** (the in-scope set exactly; function owner, `prosecdef`, `proconfig`, body without `current_setting(`/`set_config(`; a best-effort scan that no other trigger function assigns an STD column; the planted-forgery matrix with positive controls) and records the measured per-row cost in its PR report (estimate: low single-digit to about 10 µs; more than 25 µs per row reopens the choice). TASK-037, which depends on TASK-024, applies it verbatim in its first migration that creates a runtime-writable STD table and reports BLOCKED otherwise — **due before TASK-037 merges**, with the security sign-off it already carries. TASK-100 extends the function for `deleted_by`. (4) **Sketch corrections** found while checking the guard against the data model: the `number_sequences` allocation `UPDATE` (§6.4; its §4.4 column grant already listed `updated_at, updated_by, version`) and the `idempotency_keys` takeover/complete statements (§6.2) left `version` unchanged and would have been rejected; they now stamp. The outbox relay (§6.1), the guest claim (§4.3) and the saga-step sketch already stamp or elide with `…`; §7.6 item 4 says that raw SQL on an STD table stamps the columns itself. (5) **Interactions** (data-model §7.6): tenant tables carry no audit triggers and the audit tables are excluded, so the §5.4 head-row lock window is unchanged; the function reads no table, so it evaluates no policy, takes no lock and is no existence oracle (PostgreSQL enforces `WITH CHECK` after BEFORE ROW triggers); `ENABLE` (origin), not `ALWAYS`, so logical-replication apply and `pg_restore --disable-triggers` still work; `ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE`, `MERGE` and multi-row statements are checked per row.
- **Why:** The extension covers the ORM path only. One developer error in a raw statement could forge attribution and the optimistic-lock counter that the audit-ready claim and NFR-DATA-003 lean on, and the database enforced none of it (RLS stops only `org_id`). The guard is the only option that also covers definer functions, migrations and future writers; it costs one function call per written row and rides existing machinery (manifest, renderer, catalog tests, the TASK-037 template precedent of `app-is-operator.sql`). A lint inspects text only, needs a writers manifest to govern and contends for the ESLint lock; acceptance alone leaves a standing caveat on the audit-ready claim.
- **Alternatives:** documented acceptance in §7.6 only (rejected: no backstop); the raw-DML lint (rejected above); a guard that fills the columns (rejected: hides defects and overrides the `NOT NULL`-without-default contract that `catalog-std` pins); `AFTER STATEMENT` on transition tables (rejected: rows already written, one trigger per event, no gain at 1–30 rows per ORM statement); a guard that also bounds timestamps (rejected: application-clock `updated_at` against database `now()` skew would reject legitimate writes); exempting counter tables such as `number_sequences` (rejected: one uniform rule beats an exemption list, and the grant already expects the stamps).
- **Reversibility:** High — one function and one trigger per table, removable by a migration; the extension is unchanged.

### D-ARCH-092 · 2026-11-13 · principal-architect · PR #26 reviews: data-model §7.6 made exact (equal-`orgId` tolerance, `upsert`, relation fields refused, raw SQL outside the extension, application-clock `updated_at`, extension order) and ADR-0009 amendment 1 item 2 (UUIDv7: 73 / 42 unpredictable bits, never a capability)
- **Decision:** (1) data-model §7.6 (amendment of 2026-11-13) states what the extension does, as implemented and as both reviews accepted it: the server-controlled set (`deletedAt`/`deletedBy` join with TASK-100); refusal as 400 `VALIDATION_ERROR` / `UNKNOWN_FIELD` **before any statement** for every payload of the six write operations and both `upsert` branches, with the transaction rolled back; the only tolerated input is an `orgId` on create or `upsert.create` equal (case-insensitive, no trim) to the transaction's organisation, always refused on update and in an organisation-less transaction; **every relation field is refused, including `connect`/`disconnect`** (`DbError` 500 `NESTED_WRITE_UNSUPPORTED`; PR26-SEC-01, taken in PR #26's fix cycle; `connect` needs a schema-derived per-model allow-list and an amendment); raw SQL is outside the extension (the guard of D-ARCH-091 covers it); `created_at` is the database clock and `updated_at` the application clock, so `updated_at < created_at` is possible by the skew, causal order is `version`, and nothing may assume otherwise; `serverStamped` does not catch a spread, so the run-time refusal stays primary; the standard-columns extension is applied last (innermost) and TASK-100's extensions wrap it. (2) ADR-0009 amendment 1 item 2: `uuid` 14 `v7()` gives **73 unpredictable bits at a new millisecond and 42 within the same millisecond** (the "74" comment was wrong), CSPRNG-backed, strictly ascending per process and ordered across processes by millisecond only; ids are identifiers, never capabilities (guest access is a hashed 256-bit token, RLS decides the rest); creation-millisecond disclosure by public ids is accepted; the reserved actors are valid UUIDv7, so `isUuidV7` must never authenticate an externally supplied id; PostgreSQL's `uuidv7()` is documented only as "millisecond timestamp + sub-millisecond timestamp + random", so nothing relies on it beyond uniqueness and rough order. (3) TASK-100 sheet line (extension order, `deleted_*`, guard extension, `where.version`, optional database-clock `updated_at`).
- **Why:** §7.6 still read "rejects any of these fields if present" while the reviewed code tolerates the equal `orgId`, handles `upsert`, refuses nested writes and leaves raw SQL and clocks unstated (code review n2, n7; security PR26-SEC-01, -08); the entropy statement is a wrong number in a security-relevant comment (PR26-SEC-05).
- **Alternatives:** keep `connect`/`disconnect` allowed with a schema-test allow-list now (rejected: the runtime data model has no `relationFromFields`, and no repository needs a relation field — D-TASK032-02 already prescribes unchecked scalar-FK inputs); move `updated_at` onto the database clock in this fold (rejected: changes the contract PR #26 pins; left as a TASK-100 option).
- **Reversibility:** High (text).

### D-ARCH-093 · 2026-11-13 · principal-architect · PR #24 code review r2 R2-n1..n3: data-model §5.2 squat removal path per object kind, TASK-090 runbook, guard cost note (TASK-024), exemption rename-proofing for the next guard version — `90-audit-ddl-guard.sql` is not edited
- **Decision:** (1) **R2-n1.** data-model §5.2 (amendment of 2026-11-13) records that "dropping the squat still passes" holds only for type (enum, range/multirange), domain, composite type, sequence, procedure and aggregate squats (probes S1, S4, S5, S7, E8, E9); table, view, materialised view, index and function squats are refused by the `sql_drop` branch for every role but the audit owner (S2, S3, S6, E6, E7) and need a superuser to suspend `platform_audit_ddl_guard_drop`, drop, and `ENABLE ALWAYS` again in one transaction, followed by the C14 `evtenabled = 'A'` check, `ensure_audit_partitions(3)` and a readiness `ok`. Carried by a new runbook `docs/07-ops/runbooks/audit-partition-squat.md` (TASK-090 sheet, rehearsed on a local database); TASK-033 pins one table-squat `DROP` refusal and probes the unprobed rename-away path, adding the result to the table. PR #24 is not asked to change `90-*.sql` for a comment (a new blob needs a new rule-12 approval); its optional integration pin stays optional. (2) **R2-n2.** The post-state invariant roughly doubles migrator DDL time (600 statements, PGlite: 1.49 s with the r1 guard, 2.78–3.09 s with the head guard) — accepted; a TASK-024 note: the up-down-up driver report records the guard's share of `migrate deploy`; if it exceeds 25 % or `migrate deploy` exceeds 60 s in CI, the next guard version prefilters by name prefix (`LIKE 'audit\_%'`) before the regex. (3) **R2-n3.** The routine arm exempts the guard through `to_regprocedure('platform.audit_ddl_guard()')`, which is NULL — the arm then matches nothing, failing open — if the guard is renamed; only the bootstrap superuser can rename it, so it is not migrator-exploitable. "Changing the guard later" gains: exempt by `IS DISTINCT FROM` the end-trigger's `evtfoid`, or raise when the lookup is NULL; until then TASK-116's hourly tripwire also asserts `to_regprocedure('platform.audit_ddl_guard()') IS NOT NULL`.
- **Why:** An operator who meets `audit_partition_squatted` for a table squat must not discover mid-incident that the documented "drop it" fails; the cost and rename items are cheap to record and expensive to rediscover.
- **Alternatives:** edit the header comment of `90-*.sql` (rejected: new blob, new rule-12 approval, for a comment); permit migrator `DROP` of audit-named table squats (rejected: it is exactly the primitive the guard exists to refuse).
- **Reversibility:** High (text and a runbook).

### D-ARCH-094 · 2026-11-13 · principal-architect · PR #30 code review R1-m4/R1-m6 and security PR30-SEC-06: the anchor writer (TASK-116) owns `putIfAbsent` retry semantics; own credential and bucket for the anchor sink; AWS 409 `ConditionalRequestConflict` is retryable; worker role reads `anchors/`; ADR-0021 amendment 2
- **Decision:** (1) **Owner.** The F-10 follow-up is re-routed from TASK-021 (the SQL bootstrap lane, which writes no anchors) to **TASK-116**, whose sheet carries the three conditions: a lost response followed by 412 returns `created: false` and the writer compares `head().sha256` with the digest of its own line (equal: written; different or absent: `ANCHOR_SINK_MISMATCH`, never an overwrite; `sha256` is unverified metadata, the verifier's byte-exact table/sink comparison stays the control); AWS 409 `ConditionalRequestConflict` is retryable with jittered backoff inside the 15-minute window and never success; own credential and bucket. (2) **Credential and exposure.** The sink is `Pick<ObjectStorage, 'putIfAbsent' | 'head' | 'get'>` built from its own secret references and the `audit-anchors` bucket, exposed as a worker-only `anchorSink` member of `RuntimeServices`; `RuntimeServices.storage` (the existing client, documents) is exposed in PR #30's fix cycle or by TASK-147 and is never used for anchors; the port types are re-exported from `@platform/api/runtime` by the same consumer. (3) **IAM wording.** "Worker role `s3:PutObject` only" is corrected in ADR-0021 amendment 1/2, ADR-0007 amendment 7 item 7 and data-model §5.5: `PutObject` plus `GetObject` and `ListBucket` on the `anchors/` prefix (the hourly verifier already reads the sink; the writer's compare reads it too), no delete, no bypass, no retention or legal-hold permission. (4) ADR-0021 amendment 2 holds the threat note (409 shape: HTTP 409, code `ConditionalRequestConflict`, concurrent conditional write in flight, retry allowed; RustFS cannot produce it; contract suite against real S3 before G4-production). (5) TASK-116 sheet line, `x` + PR30-SEC-06, D-ARCH-093, D-ARCH-094.
- **Why:** A routed item without an owner AC is dropped silently (standing pattern); TASK-021 does not write anchors. The security review found the single shared credential could overwrite and delete an anchor on RustFS, and the IAM sentence contradicted the verifier's own sink read.
- **Alternatives:** compare bytes with `get()` instead of `head()` (rejected as the default: the retry runs inside the 15-minute window and `head` is enough to stop retrying; the verifier reads bytes anyway); expose only a documents `storage` and let TASK-116 reuse it (rejected: one credential for every bucket defeats the sink's tamper evidence at M5).
- **Reversibility:** High (wording, a sheet line and a type).

### D-SEC-PR30-02 · 2026-11-13 · security-analyst (logged by orchestrator) · PR #30 r2 delta: C1 closed
- **Decision:** PR #30 security r2 at 5f45a8b = PASS_WITH_FOLLOW-UPS; **C1 (PR30-SEC-01) closed** (silent store: 15 s put/putIfAbsent/get and 5 s head/delete/checkBucket deadlines hold without a caller signal; request timeout throws; trickling body cut at 15 s; byte-counted 5 MiB cap; retries only PUT/HEAD/GET/DELETE ≤ 3 attempts); PR30-SEC-05 and the adapter parts of -02/-03 closed (RustFS: forced `text/plain` + attachment, `BadDigest` stores nothing, forged metadata claim refused by `get`). Open: PR30-SEC-04 config half → TASK-014; INFO 06/07/08(e); new INFO PR30-SEC-09 (disposition `trim()`/filename text), -10 (`contentLength` header-or-0, SDK checksum errors → UNEXPECTED, echoed checksum not asserted), -11 (`StorageConfigError` uncaught on this branch; after the PR #20 union `installProcessErrorHandlers` must stay above `createRuntimeServices`). ADR-0021 am. 2 item 3 must say: compare `head().checksumSha256`, fall back to `get().sha256`, never the metadata `head().sha256` (proven on RustFS with a pre-seeded attacker object) — SHEET-FOLD-4.
- **Reversibility:** High.

### D-ARCH-096 · 2026-11-13 · principal-architect · PR #30 security r2 R2.5 / D-SEC-PR30-02 and code review r2 R2.4, R2.9: the anchor writer's `created: false` check compares the store-verified `head().checksumSha256`, falls back to the `sha256` that `get()` recomputed over the bytes, and never reads the metadata `head().sha256`; the writer's sink wrapper offers `isWritten(key, digest)` only; ADR-0021 amendment 2 items 3 and 4 replaced and item 6 (fail-closed credential pair for the `s3:` sink) added
- **Decision:** (1) On `putIfAbsent` → `created: false` the anchor writer asks `isWritten(key, digest)`. The wrapper calls `head()` and compares `checksumSha256` (the SHA-256 the store verified at write; lowercase hex) with the digest of the line the run built; when that is absent (object not written through the port, or a composite checksum the adapter drops) it calls `get()` and compares the `sha256` the adapter recomputed over the bytes. `head().sha256` — a metadata claim written by whoever can `PutObject` on the key — is never read. Equal = written. Different, absent after the 412, or `get()` throwing `INTEGRITY_MISMATCH`/`TOO_LARGE` = `ANCHOR_SINK_MISMATCH` (alert, never an overwrite, never retried as transient); `UNAVAILABLE` is retried inside the 15-minute window. The writer passes its digest as `sha256` to `putIfAbsent` so the store verifies it on receipt. The writer's wrapper has exactly `putIfAbsent` and `isWritten`; the verifier's has exactly `read(key)` → bytes; no `head` is reachable from `anchor.ts` or `verify.ts` (type-level test + grep test). (2) Item 4's "until that lands it is `UNEXPECTED`" is withdrawn: PR #30 (head `5f45a8b`, merge pending) maps 409 `ConditionalRequestConflict` and 400 `RequestTimeout` to `UNAVAILABLE`, `BadDigest` to `INTEGRITY_MISMATCH`, `ExpiredToken` to `ACCESS_DENIED`; `ACCESS_DENIED`, `INTEGRITY_MISMATCH` and `INVALID_ARGUMENT` fail the run closed and are not retried. (3) Item 6 (new): when `AUDIT_ANCHOR_SINK` is an `s3:` URL its two worker-only secret references (`AUDIT_ANCHOR_SINK_ACCESS_KEY_ID_REF`, `AUDIT_ANCHOR_SINK_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY_REF`) must both resolve or both be unset; exactly one is a start-up refusal naming the keys (config guard exit 78 through the shared `CREDENTIAL_PAIRS` table of TASK-014, composition throw as defence in depth, before any client, pool or queue exists); unset anchor references never fall back to `STORAGE_*`; both are refused in staging and production; the anchor bucket differs from `STORAGE_BUCKET_DOCUMENTS`. The `file:` sink needs no credentials. Folded into ADR-0021 am. 2 items 3, 4, 6, the TASK-116 line (`plan-data.mjs`, regenerated `WAVE-03.md`), data-model §5.5 and §12 A24; `rulings/wave-0-sheet-fold-3.md` row (6) carries a pointer.
- **Why:** On the pinned RustFS a key pre-seeded with other bytes and a metadata claim equal to the writer's digest makes `head().sha256` equal the digest, `head().checksumSha256` differ and `get()` throw `INTEGRITY_MISMATCH`; the old rule would have reported "written" and stopped retrying while the sink held the attacker's bytes until the verifier's byte-exact comparison noticed. A wrapper that cannot return a hash makes the rule a type, not a convention.
- **Alternatives:** keep `head().sha256` and rely on the verifier (rejected: the writer's success would be wrong in the meantime); always `get()` (rejected as the default: anchors are small but the store-verified checksum is free and already on the head response, `get()` stays the fallback); expose `head` and forbid `.sha256` by lint (rejected: the ESLint lock is TASK-020's and a type is stronger).
- **Reversibility:** High.

### D-ARCH-097 · 2026-11-13 · principal-architect · PR #30 security r2 PR30-SEC-02/-07/-09/-10 and code review r1 n2, r2 flags: ADR-0021 amendment 3 — the download path's real controls, `allowInline` closed, one disposition builder, one key builder, metadata budget; TASK-147 owns the contract, TASK-162 tests it, TASK-014 supplies the `nosniff` vhost, TASK-020 adds the ESLint SDK boundary
- **Decision:** (1) The Platform cannot add a header to a pre-signed response and RustFS sends no `X-Content-Type-Options`; the controls are the forced `response-content-type` (the type stored at put time from the detected format), forced `attachment`, and a store host that never receives the host-only `__Host-` cookies; `nosniff` is defence in depth added by a response-headers layer where one exists (Compose `edge` store vhost, CloudFront response-headers policy at M5). Amendment 1 item 2 and Decision 4 are read accordingly. Compose shares `localhost` with the apps (cookies ignore ports) with synthetic data only: accepted. (2) `allowInline: true` with an active content type is the XSS-by-document path: the documents module owns one facade `presignDownload(document, ttl)` as the only `presignGet` caller, reading bucket/key/`versionId`/type from the RLS-visible row and never setting `allowInline`; a repository test fails on `allowInline` outside `platform/storage`; a future inline preview needs an ADR amendment, an allow-list of passive types (`application/pdf`, `image/png`, `image/jpeg`) and a security record. (3) One pure `attachmentDisposition(name)` (`filename` ASCII fallback + `filename*=UTF-8''…`) from server-held text only; the port's disposition check is ASCII-anchored (no Unicode `trim`) and refuses `inline` after the type. (4) One typed key builder is the only constructor of key strings; the port rejects `.`/empty/trailing-`/` segments, caps user metadata at 2048 bytes before any I/O, and has one bucket predicate. (5) Result precision (PR30-SEC-10) rides the same adapter edit. (6) TASK-020 adds the ESLint `no-restricted-imports` entry for `@aws-sdk/*`, `@smithy/signature-v4`, `aws-sdk` outside `platform/storage` (PR30-SEC-08 (e)). Folded into ADR-0021 am. 3, the TASK-147, TASK-162, TASK-014 and TASK-020 lines, and platform.md §2.2.
- **Why:** The reviews found the `nosniff` promise had no delivery point and `allowInline` plus caller-built disposition text were the two ways a stored document becomes a page; an allow-list and a single builder remove the review burden from every future caller. There is no M1 inline use, so the cheapest safe design is no inline at all.
- **Alternatives:** a deny-list of active types (rejected: a new active or `+xml` type passes it); building `filename*` inside the adapter from a `filename` field (equivalent; the helper keeps `contentDisposition` stable for the PR #30 contract and TASK-162 can still move it inside); a CDN-only `nosniff` claim without the forced-type control (rejected: the direct store port is reachable locally and in tests).
- **Reversibility:** High.

### D-ARCH-098 · 2026-11-13 · principal-architect · PR #31 reviews (PR31-SEC-01/-02/-03/-04/-05, code review M1/M2/M3/N1/N2), D-ORCH-038 (2), PR24-SEC-04/PR26-SEC-07/PR30-SEC-08 (a)(c): TASK-015 gains one `tools/quality` + `tools/ci` hardening line, a lane A tree invariant, a `--checkpoint` narrowing (due before the `v0.1.0-m0` tag), a temp-cleanup check and the CODEOWNERS/runner-image completeness line; the G3 checklist gains items 23 and 24
- **Decision:** (1) **Submodule flag:** `--ignore-submodules=none` on every `git diff` and `git status` call of `tools/quality` and `tools/ci` (check-evidence ×3, `lib/host.mjs` ×2, check-migration-immutability, check-security-owned-paths ×2, check-porcelain), enforced by a repo test over the argument lists, plus the `.gitmodules ignore = all` tests of PR31-SEC-01; (b) test gaps of PR31-SEC-03; (c) M1 scrub prefix ends at a path boundary; (d) M3 spaced profile names; (e) N1 env-values mutant; (f) a **verifier-side** count-only host-path scan in `check-evidence` using the belt's own shapes (shared constants, so an honest run cannot match) — required, not optional — and the exotic spellings closed or pinned as named limits. (2) **Tree invariant** (PR31-SEC-02): `tools/ci/check-tree-modes.mjs`, base-ref copy, `git ls-tree -r -z` of the head: no 120000, no 160000, 100755 only on `tools/hooks/*` (code-owned allow-list), required gate (`CI_REQUIRED_GATES`). (3) **G3 checklist** (PR31-SEC-04, PR23-SEC-02 ruling 5): TEST-STRATEGY §15 item 23 (pending entries empty or each `decision` resolves to a `### D-…` heading deferring that case; no SEC-TC ID lost since W0-ACT-1) and item 24 (the transcript is a `--profile gate` run from `main`, no `--checkpoint`, not `--event push`; a `skipped` transcript is not evidence; host-path scan 0); §9.3 and README follow; the gate table of every evidence commit carries the two D-SEC-PR31-01 rows. (4) **M2 ruled: `--checkpoint` narrowing.** `check-evidence --profile gate --checkpoint Wave-0 exit|v0.1.0-m0|G3` (default G3; other profiles exit 2) narrows both the pending-entry reach and gate rule 5, the latter through a new optional manifest field `required_from` (same values, default `G3`, set by qa-lead); the `v0.1.0-m0` R0 regression passes `v0.1.0-m0`, G3 passes nothing; due before the tag. The alternative — a decision ID on every G3 entry plus a `deferred_at_gate` row for every later suite — is rejected. (5) **Temp cleanup** (D-ORCH-038): `tools/repo/temp-cleanup.test.ts` (TypeScript compiler API; deletion calls may not target `tmpdir()`/`TEMP`/`TMP`/`/tmp` directly or through one alias; `mkdtemp`-derived targets pass; waivers by exact path in a code-owned JSON); lock-owner re-verification stays an orchestrator procedure. (6) **CODEOWNERS/runner images:** the paths of PR24-SEC-04 and PR26-SEC-07 plus `apps/api/src/platform/storage/`, bootstrap-file immutability (PR #24 R1-m3), and the RustFS digest in `testcontainers_images` (read from `storage/tests/rustfs.ts` by a test). Deadlines: M2 before the `v0.1.0-m0` tag; items 1, 2 and the G3 rows before G3; items 5 and 6 before the Wave-0-exit activation PR. All of `tools/quality/**`, `tools/ci/**` and CODEOWNERS are owned paths: one security record per PR.
- **Why:** The `.gitmodules` hole is a property of every `git diff`/`git status` the tooling runs, not of one line; the tree invariant removes the root cause with plumbing nothing can filter. M2 had a second half the review did not name: gate rule 5 would also fail the tag on every suite whose owning task has not merged, so narrowing only the pending entries would have left the tag unrunnable. The verifier-side scan turns a self-reported scrub into a checked one at no false-positive cost.
- **Alternatives:** the decision-ID route for M2 (rejected: dozens of manifest rows and a security record per tag); the scrub-only control (rejected: PR31-SEC-05's point is that the verifier does not look); a lint rule instead of a repo test for the submodule flag (rejected: ESLint lock, and the arrays are data).
- **Reversibility:** High.

### D-ARCH-099 · 2026-11-13 · principal-architect · PR #24 security r2 PR24-SEC-10 (LOW) and PR24-SEC-11 (INFO): the `CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY` leftover is a stated limit with a recovery and a test; migration files may not contain top-level transaction control (rule 11 sub-clause (c)); `90-audit-ddl-guard.sql` is not edited
- **Decision:** (1) data-model §5.2 gains a second 2026-11-13 amendment: a refused CIC under an audit name leaves a committed `indisvalid = false` migrator-owned index (the build phases commit before `ddl_command_end`), after which every other DDL by the migrator is refused by the end-of-command invariant and `DROP INDEX` by `sql_drop` even for a superuser; reach = the migrator credential outside the linted lane; no guard change (an event trigger gets no object identity at `ddl_command_start`). Recovery: one leftover — as the migrator `ALTER INDEX … RENAME TO <non-audit name>; DROP INDEX …`; two or more — the cluster superuser, in one transaction, `SET LOCAL event_triggers = off; DROP INDEX …; COMMIT;` and re-check `evtenabled = 'A'` on both event triggers (unproven on RDS until COND-G4-PROD M5 check (d)). Two earlier statements are corrected: the fold-3 R2-n1 break-glass "needs no suspension" holds only for the last squat, and "the migrator cannot create a squat" has this one exception. Owners: TASK-090 runbook section, TASK-033 clone-database case family (CIC cannot run in a transaction block). (2) §8.3 rule 11 gains sub-clause (c): a top-level transaction-control statement (`BEGIN`, `START TRANSACTION`, `COMMIT`, `END`, `ROLLBACK`, `ABORT`, `SAVEPOINT`, `RELEASE`, `ROLLBACK TO`, `PREPARE TRANSACTION`, `COMMIT PREPARED`, `ROLLBACK PREPARED`) is refused in `migration.sql` and `down.sql`; owner TASK-024, with the DO-body RESET asymmetry and the setter-key half. TASK-033 also takes PR27-SEC-02 (C14 and the immutability suite assert the product state: no `audit_entries` RLS row, `tgenabled`/`evtenabled` = `A`; a planted origin-mode enable fails C14).
- **Why:** The leftover is availability only, the actor holds equivalent levers, and nothing in the guard can undo committed index-build phases; stating the limit and rehearsing the recovery is the whole fix. Refusing transaction control is cheaper and sounder than tracking `lock_timeout` across `BEGIN … ROLLBACK`, `SAVEPOINT` and `ROLLBACK TO` in a text linter; migrations are applied statement by statement and have no use for them.
- **Alternatives:** a guard version that parses `current_query()` at `ddl_command_start` (rejected: fragile, and a changed blob needs a new rule-12 approval); tracking values through transaction blocks (rejected above); doing nothing about the INFO (rejected: the next file inherits a raised `lock_timeout`).
- **Reversibility:** High.
