### D-TASK019-01 · 2026-11-13 · backend-developer / senior-developer · SPK-05 verdict GO: RustFS 1.0.4 pinned; no SeaweedFS fallback (TASK-019)
- **Decision:** RustFS `rustfs/rustfs:1.0.4@sha256:ed9210d6411d77ffceb70d94b964a3cb7d225983368bc25bebe01e995293dcc2` (pushed 2026-10-25; 1.0.5 of 2026-11-10 was inside the 7-day cooldown) is the pinned Testcontainers image, shared by the contract and health suites through `apps/api/src/platform/storage/tests/rustfs.ts`. SPK-05 is GO: path-style addressing, pre-signed GET with `response-content-disposition` and enforced expiry (403 after the TTL), versioning (distinct `VersionId`s, reads by version), HEAD user metadata (`x-amz-meta-sha256`), conditional `If-None-Match: *` (412 → `created: false`, original kept) and the SDK 3.1162 default CRC32 flexible checksums all behave as on AWS S3. ADR-0021 and A-084 stand; no amendment request.
- **Why:** The exit criterion of R-ARCH-05 / SPK-05 is the adapter contract test green on RustFS; it is (13 tests).
- **Alternatives:** SeaweedFS fallback (not needed); `requestChecksumCalculation: 'WHEN_REQUIRED'` (not needed; the contract suite is the tripwire after any RustFS or SDK bump).
- **Reversibility:** High (one image constant behind the `ObjectStorage` port).

### D-TASK019-02 · 2026-11-13 · backend-developer / senior-developer · `object_storage` readiness and the S3 adapter's error and retry policy (TASK-019)
- **Decision:** (1) The `object_storage` readiness component is `HeadBucket` on `STORAGE_BUCKET_DOCUMENTS` through the port (`health/checks/object-storage.ts`), bounded by the runner's 2 s abort signal; the `pendingCheck('object_storage')` stub and its tripwire test are removed in the same commit (PR #9 m2, D-TASK006-02, D-ARCH-074); the audit stubs stay for TASK-021. (2) SDK failures become `ObjectStorageError` with a fixed message: 403 → `ACCESS_DENIED`; network, abort, timeout, 5xx/408/429 → `UNAVAILABLE`; everything else (including a missing bucket) → `UNEXPECTED`; 404 on an object → `undefined`. The SDK message, endpoint, bucket, key and credentials are never copied. (3) Every call: connect timeout 2 s, request timeout 10 s, `maxAttempts` 3 (SDK standard jittered retry); bounded further by D-TASK019-03. A retried `putIfAbsent` whose first attempt succeeded but lost its response reports `created: false` (F-10, now pinned by a loopback test). (4) `put` takes bytes ≤ 5 MiB (ADR-0021 am. 2); `get` refuses to buffer larger objects. Streaming and multipart uploads wait for exports (M2). (5) `createRuntimeServices` takes the resolved `secrets`; static credentials are used only when both `STORAGE_*_REF` resolve, neither selects the SDK default chain (IAM task role at M5); exactly one is refused (D-TASK019-03). (6) A boundary unit test keeps `@aws-sdk/client-s3` / `s3-request-presigner` imports inside `apps/api/src/platform/storage/` (ADR-0021 §1), instead of a new ESLint entry (the `lint` lock belongs to TASK-020 in this batch).
- **Why:** AT-US-012-02/05 (no endpoint or credential in bodies or logs), CLAUDE.md §9 (timeouts, retries on idempotent operations only, typed configuration).
- **Alternatives:** A pass-through `ok` stub until compose has RustFS (rejected: the sheet requires the real check now). Local consequence: until TASK-014 adds the compose `rustfs` service and bucket-init job, a local stack reports `object_storage: unavailable` (routed to TASK-014).
- **Reversibility:** High.

### D-TASK019-03 · 2026-11-13 · senior-developer · PR #30 fix cycle 1: time bounds, integrity, presign and credential hardening of the S3 adapter (TASK-019)
- **Decision:** (1) PR30-SEC-01 / R1-m1/m2: the SDK handler runs with `throwOnRequestTimeout: true`; every operation is bounded by `AbortSignal.any([callerSignal, AbortSignal.timeout(deadline)])` with 15 s for put/putIfAbsent/get (all attempts, backoff and body) and 5 s for head/delete/checkBucket; any failure after the bounded signal fired is `UNAVAILABLE`; `get` counts bytes while reading (5 MiB cap without relying on `Content-Length`). Pinned by `s3ClientConfig` unit assertions plus a loopback-server suite (silent server, trickling body, 3 attempts on 5xx, F-10). (2) R1-m4: error names are consulted before the status: `RequestTimeout` (400) and `ConditionalRequestConflict` (409) → `UNAVAILABLE`; `ExpiredToken`, `TokenRefreshRequired`, `CredentialsProviderError` → `ACCESS_DENIED`; `BadDigest` → `INTEGRITY_MISMATCH`; `RequestTimeTooSkewed` dropped from the retryable names (403 `ACCESS_DENIED`). (3) PR30-SEC-03 (adapter part): put sends `ChecksumSHA256` (store-verified); `get` returns the SHA-256 recomputed over the bytes and refuses a body that contradicts the metadata claim; `head` exposes the store's checksum as `checksumSha256` and documents metadata `sha256` as an unverified claim. (4) PR30-SEC-02 (adapter part): `presignGet` requires `responseContentType` (a token-only media type) and refuses any disposition type other than `attachment`, `inline` only with `allowInline: true`. (5) PR30-SEC-04 (adapter part) / R1-m5: exactly one resolved `STORAGE_*_REF` throws `StorageConfigError` (key names only) before any pool or client is created, so the process fails to start instead of using the host's default identity; a readiness failure is logged as `object_storage.error` `{ error: <ObjectStorageError code> }` only. (6) R1-m7: the boundary test denies every `@aws-sdk/*` package and `@smithy/signature-v4` outside `platform/storage` (other AWS adapters need an explicit folder entry) over `.ts/.tsx/.mts/.cts/.js/.mjs/.cjs`; the unit test is the control (no ESLint entry while TASK-020 holds the lint lock). (7) R1-m3: the signing instant is floored to the second, so `expiresAt` equals the store's real expiry. (8) ADR-0021 am. 2 item 5 (D-ARCH-093/094): `RuntimeServices.storage` exposes the documents storage and `@platform/api/runtime` re-exports the port types (not the adapter); SPK-05 routes the F-10 anchor follow-up to TASK-116 and names `head().checksumSha256` (store-verified) rather than the metadata claim for its comparison.
- **Why:** CLAUDE.md §9 (every external call has a timeout; the SDK default request timeout only warns), security review PR-0030 condition C1 and LOW findings 02/03/04, code review R1-m1..m5, m7.
- **Alternatives:** A single 30 s deadline for every operation (rejected: readiness-like calls should fail fast); `filename`-only disposition built inside the adapter (deferred to the document download task, TASK-162, with the route test); a config guard and hardened-environment rule for the credential pair (TASK-014, routed); logging only on state change (rejected: the readiness runner already limits evaluations to one per second per process).
- **Reversibility:** High (adapter-internal; the port gained optional fields and one required presign field before any caller exists).

### D-TASK032-01 · 2026-11-13 · senior-developer · Standard-columns extension bound per transaction, not through AsyncLocalStorage (TASK-032)
- **Decision:** `withTenantTx` gains an optional `scopeClient(stamp)` dependency; the runtime composition passes `(stamp) => withStandardColumns(client, stamp)`, which calls `client.$extends(...)` once per transaction with the validated `{ orgId, actorId }` (the `app.org_id` / `app.actor_id` values of the context statement) and opens the interactive transaction on the extended client. The extension only rewrites args and calls `query(args)`; which columns a model has is read from the client's runtime data model (cached per root client), so new models need no registry edit. An empty actor is stamped as the reserved ANONYMOUS actor (data-model §1.6).
- **Why:** data-model §7.6 requires the context to come from the `withTenantTx` closure (no AsyncLocalStorage) and ADR-0005 am. 10 item 5 / SPK-03 F-05 run `withTenantTx` on the extended client. A query extension has no access to the transaction identity, so a per-transaction `$extends` (Prisma's own per-request pattern; it shares engine and pool) is the only closure-scoped binding.
- **Alternatives:** Store the stamp in the existing re-entrance AsyncLocalStorage (rejected: contradicts data-model §7.6); stamp inside the `TenantDb` guard (rejected: the sheet and ADR name a Prisma client extension, and the guard is a security boundary that should stay read-only); one static extension reading `app.*` back from the database (rejected: an extra query per write and the extension must not query).
- **Reversibility:** High (one dependency of `createWithTenantTx`; without it the database's `NOT NULL` server columns reject inserts).

### D-TASK032-02 · 2026-11-13 · senior-developer · Server fields in repository input are 400 UNKNOWN_FIELD; `serverStamped` typed seam; nested writes refused (TASK-032)
- **Decision:** (1) A create/update/upsert payload that carries `id`, `createdAt`, `updatedAt`, `createdBy`, `updatedBy`, `version` or `onBehalfOfOrgId` (and `orgId` on update, or an `orgId` other than the transaction's on create) is rejected before any statement with `AppError('VALIDATION_ERROR')` whose issues are `UNKNOWN_FIELD` at `/body/<snake_name>` (AT-US-064-03, EC-A18); the same list (`SERVER_CONTROLLED_FIELDS`) and issue builder (`serverControlledFieldIssues`) live in `@platform/shared` for the request-validation slot (TASK-020). (2) Prisma generates `createdBy`/`updatedBy` (and tenant `orgId`) as required create fields because the columns have no default; repositories write `data: serverStamped<Prisma.XUncheckedCreateInput>({ ... })`, which removes every server column from the accepted type and returns the value unchanged. (3) Relation-field writes are refused with `DbError` 500 `NESTED_WRITE_UNSUPPORTED` (amended by D-TASK032-04: every relation field, `connect`/`disconnect` included), because Prisma runs no query extension for nested rows. (4) `version: { increment: 1 }` on every update; the version-conditional `where` and 412/409 mapping stay with TASK-100.
- **Why:** Defence in depth for mass assignment (REQ-SEC-007) without trusting the HTTP layer; a typed seam instead of `as` casts scattered over repositories; failing closed on writes that would escape the stamping.
- **Alternatives:** Silently overwrite forged fields (rejected: hides mass-assignment bugs and AT-US-064-03 asks for 400); add database defaults to `created_by` (rejected: server-set columns must not default, catalog-std); recursive stamping of nested writes (deferred until a use case needs it).
- **Reversibility:** High.

### D-TASK032-03 · 2026-11-13 · senior-developer · `catalog-std` schema rules and exemptions; AT-US-064-06/07 left to their generators (TASK-032)
- **Decision:** New suite `prisma/tests/catalog/standard-columns.int.test.ts` (rules in `standard-columns-scans.ts`): no `timestamp without time zone` in `public`/`platform`/`audit` (AT-US-064-04); every `date` column has a sibling `text` `time_zone` / `*_time_zone` column (AT-US-064-05, exemption map empty); every `public` base table has the six standard columns (`id uuid` sole PK `DEFAULT uuidv7()`, `created_at`/`updated_at timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now()`, `created_by`/`updated_by uuid NOT NULL` without default, `version int NOT NULL DEFAULT 1` with a `version >= 1` or `= 1` CHECK); no identity/sequence columns; every `on_behalf_of_org_id` is a nullable uuid pinned by `CHECK (on_behalf_of_org_id IS NULL)`. Exemptions: `_prisma_migrations`, `bootstrap_migrations`; the OI-08 append-only family (`audit_entries*`, `audit_pii_vault`, `audit_checkpoint_heads`, `audit_anchors`, `outbox_events`, `processed_events`) needs only a `timestamptz NOT NULL` creation column (its keys follow ADR-0007); `audit_entries.on_behalf_of_org_id` (audit copy). The exemptions were shaped against TASK-021's `prisma/bootstrap/10-audit.sql` so both branches stay green in either merge order. AT-US-064-06 (`rbac-matrix`) and AT-US-064-07 (`audit-generator`) are delivered by TASK-027 and TASK-029/033 once a create route exists; this task provides the stamped `created_by` and null on-behalf they assert.
- **Why:** NFR-DATA-002/003 and REQ-RLS-012 are schema properties; checking the live catalogue binds every later migration.
- **Alternatives:** Extend `c01-c12` C8 (rejected: TASK-021 edits that file in parallel); exemptions in the table-class manifests (deferred: the loader is security-owned).
- **Reversibility:** High.

### D-TASK032-04 · 2026-11-13 · senior-developer · PR #26 fix cycle 1: relation fields refused, `scopeClient` required, unknown catalogue fails closed (TASK-032)
- **Decision:** Closes PR26-SEC-01, PR26-SEC-02 (code review m1, m2, m3), the DECISIONS.md repair (m4), PR26-SEC-05/06 (INFO) and code n8. (1) Every relation field in a write payload (`create`, `createMany*`, `update`, `updateMany*`, both `upsert` branches) is refused, deny by default, with `NESTED_WRITE_UNSUPPORTED`: `connect`, `disconnect`, `set`, `connectOrCreate` and every nested write alike; the `ALLOWED_NESTED_OPERATIONS` allow-list is deleted. Repositories use the unchecked create/update inputs (scalar FKs), which D-TASK032-02 already required. (2) `WithTenantTxDeps.scopeClient` is required (no `?? client` fallback); a test that wants the plain client passes `scopeClient: () => client`. A runtime wiring test builds `createDatabaseRuntime` with a recording client class and fails if `runtime.ts` stops wiring `withStandardColumns`. (3) An empty runtime data model throws `TypeError` when the extension is built, and a write on a model that is not in the catalogue is rejected (reads pass). (4) `catalog-std` exemption lookups use `Object.hasOwn`; a parity test over the generated client asserts that a field mapped to a standard column is named canonically and conversely. (5) The `uuidv7` entropy comment says 73 random bits at a new millisecond, 42 within one.
- **Why:** The security review rated the wiring and the relation form LOW but both defeat the defence silently (updates lose the version bump, a child row is written unstamped); a required dependency and a refused-by-default relation payload cannot regress quietly.
- **Alternatives:** Allow-list `connect` for named relations through a schema-derived map (deferred until a use case needs it; the runtime data model carries no `relationFromFields`); a Prisma-relation-forbidding schema test (rejected: refusing at run time covers the unchecked-input contract and the converse).
- **Reversibility:** High.

### D-ORCH-040 · 2026-11-13 · sdlc-orchestrator · Task decision blocks go to main, not PR branches
- **Decision:** Every PR that appended `D-TASKxxx-*` blocks to `docs/sdlc/DECISIONS.md` on its branch conflicted with main at each merge (append-append), forcing extra merges of main that — once lane-B suites became active — also pull non-docs code into the branch and stale the evidence. From now on, build/fix agents put their task decisions in the PR body and their Handoff Report; **the orchestrator appends them to `DECISIONS.md` on main** when the PR is opened or merged. PR branches must not edit `docs/sdlc/DECISIONS.md` (or STATUS.md). Existing open PRs that already carry blocks resolve the same way: a docs-only branch commit restoring the merge-base `DECISIONS.md`, with the orchestrator appending the blocks on main (done for PR #26 at c694583 / 4a0063c).
- **Reversibility:** High.

### D-TASK018-01 · 2026-11-13 · performance-engineer / senior-developer · SPK-04 verdict: exit NOT DEMONSTRATED (INCONCLUSIVE); R-ARCH-04 not retired; levers routed to principal-architect (reworded in fix cycle 1, code review R1-M2)
- **Decision:** One verdict: **the SPK-04 exit (Δp95 ≤ 15 ms with the per-stream advisory lock + vault inserts at 300 rps) is NOT DEMONSTRATED: INCONCLUSIVE** under TEST-STRATEGY §7.10 at 300 rps (0 of 6 arms valid, 10 invalidity reasons) and at 150 rps (both `batched` arms invalid), because the host was shared and busy. (The sheet's vocabulary is GO / FALLBACK; the verdict tool also has FALLBACK-INSUFFICIENT and INCONCLUSIVE; none of the first three is claimed, because each needs valid arms.) **Direction, not proof:** the HOT tenant (20 % share = 60 rps on one stream) queued on the stream lock in the least-disturbed 300 rps repetition (rep 2: hot lock wait p50 97.7 ms / p95 228.6 ms; Δp95 on − off +1 042 ms, `batched` − off +217 ms, with that repetition's `on` arm itself invalid), and queued transactions hold pool connections, so other tenants failed with `SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE` (2 s `maxWait`). Repetition 1 (every arm invalid, `off` itself collapsed) is evidence of host disturbance only. **R-ARCH-04 is not retired.** At 150 rps both `on` repetitions are valid, but the budget is also not demonstrated: Δp95 +22.1 / −2.3 ms (pooled +9.9 ms), Δp99 +59.4 / −149.8 ms; the clean-baseline repetition (rep 1) fails both budgets and n = 2 cannot resolve 15 ms on this host. `batched` cannot be ranked: the same configuration collapsed at 150 rps (p95 1.9–2.8 s) and did not at 300 rps rep 2 (p95 255 ms). The multi-row vault variant (SPK-04 §5.2) stays a candidate for TASK-030, subject to the `EXPLAIN` precondition of §5.4. The levers of SPK-04 §6 (a) `SELECT … FOR UPDATE` head-row lock instead of the advisory lock, (b) hot-tenant sub-streams, (c) a short audit lock wait that fails fast, (d) a native-Linux re-measure, go to principal-architect as inputs (taken up in ADR-0007 amendment 10, D-ARCH-085..090, D-ORCH-033); the clean 300 rps proof is TASK-280's (T-QA-06 `audit-ab`) before G3. Integrity held on the SPK-08 **prototype** store throughout (it proves no property of the product store):
  - 223 118 entries fully recomputed, 0 chain faults;
  - immutability returns 42501 at both the privilege and trigger layers;
  - prototype triggers, DDL guard and RLS state as installed (origin-mode triggers, RLS on `audit_entries`: the design differs, see D-TASK018-04).
- **Why:** Round trips × RTT (about 1.5 ms per statement under the lock on this host, SPK-03) is the **working hypothesis** for what caps a stream's rate, not a measurement: the harness never measures hold time, and the data need about 15 ms of hold at 300 rps against about 7.5 ms at 150 rps, so host contention or a WAL-flush floor are not excluded (SPK-04 §5.1). Counts of round trips come from the harness's own counter. The sheet's DoD sends an unmet exit to the architect.
- **Alternatives:** Declaring GO from the pooled 150 rps `on` numbers was rejected: the target rate is 300 rps and rep 1 alone fails the budget. Declaring FALLBACK / "R-ARCH-04 confirmed / exit not met" (the first wording of this entry) was rejected in review: 0 of 6 arms were valid. Re-running until the host is quiet was rejected inside the S time box. The clean 300 rps A/B (at least 5 repetitions, randomised or balanced order, median and range, hold-time and `pg_stat_statements` round-trip measurement) is routed to TASK-280.
- **Reversibility:** High. No product code changed, and the lane-B re-run revisits the verdict.

### D-TASK018-02 · 2026-11-13 · senior-developer · SPK-04 harness design: real runtime path, harness-only mode switch, file placement
- **Decision:**
  1. Traffic runs as `platform_app` through the production `createDatabaseRuntime` / `withTenantTx` (Prisma 7 + adapter-pg, tagged `$queryRaw`/`$executeRaw` on `TenantDb`). The superuser is used only for bootstrap, fixtures, seed and the post-run integrity checks.
  2. The `off|on|batched` switch exists only in the spike harness (`SPK04_AUDIT`, read at process start). The product's audit-off baseline remains the build-time `-bench` image (ADR-0007 item 4, R-12). There is no runtime flag.
  3. The recorded runs used the SPK-08 audit **prototype** (`spk08/10-audit.sql` and `90-audit-ddl-guard.sql`, reused unchanged) plus `spk04/fixtures/20-spk04-audit-write.sql` (data-model §5.7 verbatim and the `audit_stream_heads` columns), with the guard installed after all audit DDL. No bootstrap file and no migration were added. **Fix cycle 1:** PR #24 (TASK-021) deleted the prototype, so the harness now applies the real `prisma/bootstrap` lane (00..02, `10-audit.sql`, `90-audit-ddl-guard.sql`) and fixture 20 is deleted (D-ORCH-033).
  4. The DB harness lives in `prisma/tests/spikes/spk04/`, following the SPK-03/SPK-08 precedent. That directory is type-checked by `tools/tsconfig.json`, which may import `apps/api/src/platform/db`. Only the k6 script sits at the sheet path `tests/load/spikes/spk04-audit.js`. This avoided any `tsconfig*.json` change: a composite `tests/load` project cannot compile those imports (TS6307).
  5. JCS is a small, exact RFC 8785 implementation (`canonical.ts`, unit-tested), because only `packages/audit` declares `canonicalize`. No new dependency.
  6. The sheet's DoD line "throwaway code is not merged" is read as: nothing outside `prisma/tests/spikes/spk04/**` and `tests/load/spikes/**`, and nothing without a named deleting PR (D-ARCH-089, applied by D-ORCH-033 over the code reviewer's drop recommendation). The harness is **executable evidence under a lifecycle** (SPK-04 §8): `canonical.ts`, `chain.ts` and their tests are deleted by TASK-030; `server.ts`, `runner.ts`, `verdict.ts`, `paths.ts`, the tests, fixture 30 and the k6 script by TASK-280. Unlike SPK-03 / SPK-08, whose `*.int.test.ts` suites run in lane B, the runner is executed by no lane, so rot is guarded by a unit-lane tripwire (`paths.test.ts`: every path the runner reads exists, the real bootstrap still creates the tables it uses, no product code references the harness). Conditions: no import from `apps/**` or `packages/**`, no coverage, no image, `SPK04_AUDIT` harness-only.
  7. No `-bench` build profile was added (the spike has no product image). PR3-SEC-11 / SEC-TC-18 therefore stays open for the task that first builds the `-bench` image (TASK-280 lane-B `audit-ab`, or TASK-030), which must also add the `APP_ENV ∈ {local, test}` refusal in the `packages/config` guards (ADR-0018 vocabulary).
- **Why:** The brief requires measuring through the real write path without weakening immutability, the DDL guard or RLS. It also rules out new dependencies and any owned-config churn beyond the lint block of D-TASK018-03.
- **Alternatives:** Raw `pg` instead of Prisma was rejected because it would understate the per-statement overhead the product pays. Copying the SPK-08 SQL was rejected because the copy would drift. Putting the harness under `tests/load` was rejected because it needs owned tsconfig edits.
- **Reversibility:** High. The code is throwaway; its lifecycle is in SPK-04 §8.

### D-TASK018-03 · 2026-11-13 · performance-engineer / senior-developer · k6 pin, loopback binding, ESLint block for k6 scripts
- **Decision:**
  1. k6 is pinned **by digest only**: `grafana/k6@sha256:5221b620a4f874faff6e32ba597aa667c058391fe4898b1c6f6377f062c6cdec` (k6 v2.2.0, commit 00a9a1b7f5, image created 2026-08-10, so more than 7 days old). The `2.2.0` tag now resolves to a different index digest, so a `tag@digest` pin would mislead.
  2. The harness replicas bind to `127.0.0.1`. The k6 container reaches them through `host.docker.internal`, which Docker Desktop proxies to host loopback; the runs saw 0 transport errors. `0.0.0.0` was not used.
  3. One narrow `eslint.config.mjs` block for `tests/load/**/*.js` declares the k6 globals (`__ENV`, `__VU`, `__ITER`, `open`, `console`) and `import-x/core-modules: ['k6/http', 'k6/execution']`. Inline `global` comments are forbidden by the suppression policy. TASK-280 (T-QA-06) reuses the block. `eslint.config.mjs` is a security-owned path, so lane A needs a security record.
- **Why:** Supply-chain pinning (ADR-0024: k6 via Docker), least exposure on a shared laptop, and zero suppressions.
- **Alternatives:** A TypeScript k6 script was rejected because it needs k6 types, a new dependency. Binding `0.0.0.0` was rejected because of the network exposure and a firewall prompt.
- **Reversibility:** High.

### D-TASK018-04 · 2026-11-13 · performance-engineer / senior-developer · SPK-04 measurement method, A-029 re-baseline, routed findings
- **Decision:**
  1. **Method.**
     - Per rate: 2 repetitions × [off, on, batched], in that fixed order.
     - Each arm: CHECKPOINT first, 20 s warm-up (discarded), 120 s measured.
     - Δ is taken within a repetition; pooled Δ is the mean of the per-repetition Δ.
     - The fail-closed VIEW entry is written in a second short transaction before the response, which is the conservative choice.
     - Op mix: create 35 %, update 20 %, detail 30 %, list 10 %, login_failed 5 %, with a 20 % hot tenant.
     - Simplifications: the old value in an update is `[REDACTED]`; the recorded runs used the SPK-08 prototype, which had RLS on `audit_entries` (the design has none: data-model §5.2, PR12-SEC-08) and no RLS on the prototype vault and head tables; Postgres default settings; `SELECT 1` stands in for the login lookup.
     - Round trips are counted by the harness's own instrumentation (they match the statement list), not measured on the wire. n = 2 and mean-of-2 pooling cannot resolve a 15 ms budget on this host (code review R1-m1).
  2. **A-029 indication** (not a re-baseline) on this shared Windows / Docker Desktop host (i9-11950H, 16 logical CPUs, 32 GB): the full mix with audit `on` was sustained at 150 rps in 2 of 2 valid repetitions; 300 rps was not demonstrated. A clean 300 rps A/B needs a quiet or dedicated host.
  3. **Routed findings.**
     - Data-model §5.4 step 3: `'\x' || repeat('00', 32)` is `text` and fails with 42804 against bytea; use `decode(repeat('00', 32), 'hex')`. Routed to principal-architect (text amendment) and to TASK-021/TASK-030.
     - To TASK-030:
       - SQL text rules: keep multi-argument `unnest` and `extract` unqualified; bind arrays instead of `Prisma.join` on `TenantDb`. (RETURNING on the CTE insert is simply not needed; the earlier "no RETURNING under RLS" advice was specific to the prototype's RLS on `audit_entries`, which the design does not have.)
       - A budget of at most 3 round trips under the lock is a **hypothesis** (SPK-04 §5.1: the model predicts about 3 ms wait where 97.7 ms was measured); TASK-280 measures grant-to-COMMIT hold time per request and the WAL-flush share before it becomes a spec.
       - A **precondition**: an `EXPLAIN` of the batched token SELECT against a vault of ≥ 100k rows before `batched` is adopted. The two invalid 150 rps batched arms showed Postgres CPU of 67 % and 114 % (`docker stats`) with an unchanged median that could not be attributed.
     - Pool coupling (lock waiters exhaust the pool and fail other tenants): routed to TASK-025 and to principal-architect as lever (c).
     - NFR-AUDIT-005 wording (per-repetition Δ and pass rule, at least 5 repetitions, ABBA or Latin-square order, median and range, hot-stream share, VIEW transaction included; no mean-of-2 pooling): routed to principal-architect / product-manager.
     - Lane-B `audit-ab` re-run before G3: routed to TASK-280.
- **Why:** Keeps the absolute numbers indicative and the A/B comparison honest on a shared host, and gives every finding an owner.
- **Alternatives:** Randomised arm order is deferred to TASK-280. The fixed order puts `batched` last against the largest tables; this is noted as a confounder.
- **Reversibility:** High.

### D-TASK018-05 · 2026-11-13 · senior-developer · SPK-04 evidence lives outside the lane-B `runs/` tree
- **Decision:** The two SPK-04 run directories live at `docs/05-quality/performance/spikes/SPK-04/<UTC stamp>_<sha7>/`, not at `docs/05-quality/performance/runs/`. The runner's default `SPK04_OUT` matches this path.
- **Why:** TASK-011 (PR #23, merged while this PR was being prepared) made `docs/05-quality/{tests,security,performance}/runs/` the lane-B evidence tree, and `quality:check-evidence` (lane A, base-ref copy) checks it strictly: run IDs are `YYYYMMDDTHHMMZ_<sha7>`, every `summary.json` must validate against `tools/quality/summary.schema.json`, reports must be JUnit-backed, `git_dirty` must be false, and every changed run directory is evaluated. Spike evidence is not a lane-B suite run. It has no manifest suite and no JUnit, and its `summary.json` is the spike's own A/B format. Under `runs/` it fails the check, and rewriting it would mean hand-editing machine-generated evidence. The sheet's line "evidence under `docs/05-quality/performance/runs/`" predates that checker, so the spike evidence stays next to the performance area under its own `spikes/` folder. The lane-B `audit-ab` re-run (TASK-280) will produce schema-conformant `runs/` evidence.
- **Alternatives:** Convert the evidence to the heavy-run schema. Rejected: it would be hand-edited evidence, and its `git_sha` would be stale against the merged head. Put the evidence under `docs/04-plan/spikes/`. Rejected: keeping it in the performance area is closer to the sheet's intent.
- **Reversibility:** High (a directory move).

### D-ORCH-042 · 2026-11-13 · sdlc-orchestrator · Post-merge gate when a squash combines untested PR pairs
- **Decision:** When a PR squash-merges onto a main that gained other non-docs PRs after the PR's evidence base (no textual conflict, but never tested together), the orchestrator runs a post-merge gate on main (lint, typecheck, unit, api, and the integration suites of the touched areas) in a detached worktree. ### D-TASK020-01..17 · 2026-11-13 · senior-developer (with backend-developer / database-engineer specialists) · TASK-020 mandatory route metadata, pipeline skeleton, data-layer guards
- **Decision:** (01) `createApp` takes `health` and module `routes` as `defineRoute` descriptors and mounts them only through `mountRoutes`, which registers each route's final handler in a weak registry; raw routers can no longer be mounted, framework tests use `routing/tests/fixture-route.ts` and the `pipeline` slot seam. (02) Composed-app suites live in `tests/generated` (`contract-drift.test.ts` moved from tools/openapi, `api-mounts.ts` imports apps/api statically through project references, `route-metadata.ts/.test.ts`); `npm run test:contract` runs them. (03) PR8-SEC-05 (c) is one-directional plus a refinement: a signature-only permission needs `auth: signature`, and a signature route declares a signature-only permission or `public` — the contract's `receiveCarrierPush` is `public` + carrier signature, so the security record's `<=>` would reject a contract operation (security-analyst to confirm). Tenancy values are the contract's `x-tenancy`; `auth` is `anonymous | session | quote-token | signature`, derived from the operation's `security`. ### D-ARCH-102 · 2026-11-13 · principal-architect · D-TASK020-05 (PR #32): the generated Prisma 7 client is a composite TypeScript project over `prisma/generated/prisma`, packaged as `@platform/prisma/client`
- **Decision:** (1) **Produced:** unchanged (`deps:rebuild` step 3 through the verified wrapper) plus a new `npm run db:generate` (Prisma 7 no longer generates after `migrate dev`). The generator block pins `runtime = "nodejs"`, `moduleFormat = "esm"`, `generatedFileExtension = "ts"`, `importFileExtension = "js"`: the CLI otherwise infers the module format and the import extension from the nearest `tsconfig.json`, so a `module: commonjs` or `moduleResolution: bundler` edit would silently emit extension-less imports. (2) **Compiled:** `prisma/client/tsconfig.json` is composite (no references; `rootDir ../generated/prisma`, `outDir ../dist/client`, source and declaration maps off), referenced by `apps/api` and `tools`, and **not** added to the root `tsconfig.json` (verified: adding it fails `tools/repo/root-scripts.test.ts` AT-US-001-04, which pins the root list). `tools/tsconfig.json` drops `../prisma/generated/**/*.ts` from `include`, adds the reference and lists `apps/api/src/platform/db/generated.ts` in `files` (TS6307 otherwise). (3) **Packaged:** the existing `@platform/prisma` workspace; `exports` has exactly `./client` (`@platform/source`, `types`, `default`); `scripts.build = tsc -b client`; `scripts.typegen` is a presence-and-freshness check that never generates (nothing runs the Prisma CLI implicitly). `apps/api` depends on the package, `apps/worker` does not (it goes through `@platform/api/runtime`). (4) **Shipped:** images copy `prisma/package.json` and `prisma/dist/client` and never the generated TypeScript, the schema, migrations, bootstrap or seed (platform.md 3.2, 2026-11-13). (5) **Verified before ruling** in a scratch extract of PR #32 @fa67aca with the repository's `node_modules` (real 4-model client): `tsc -b` of api, worker, prisma, tools, tests/generated, tests/api and tests/contract-stubs clean; the types are real (`@ts-expect-error` held for an unknown column, `$transaction` and the SYSTEM model on `TenantDb<Prisma.TransactionClient>`; a mutant SYSTEM model name fails the conformance type); `eslint` on the new files; the Jest unit project imports the package under `@platform/source`; compiled `apps/api` imported it with no conditions, built a client over `@prisma/adapter-pg` and reached the driver; in the whole unit run the only failure attributable to the change was `runtime.test.ts` "worker and API share it", which asserts the old "no runner" state (intended; the other failures are artefacts of the extract: no `.git`, no `docs/`, no `size-limit` binary). Limits found: TS2883 for a non-async function returning a `PrismaPromise` (repository functions are async or annotated); `@ts-nocheck` is always written. Cost: 4 models cold 1.9 s; synthetic 100 models (8.4 MB, 213k lines) generate in 5 s, compile cold in 9.3 s at 390 MB, up to date in 0.27 s, 9.2 MB of output, recorded as R-ARCH-28 with trigger and fallbacks.
- **Why:** The blocker was TypeScript layout (`rootDir: src`, TS6307, `import-x/no-relative-packages`), not lint. The repository already solves this for every other package with the `@platform/source` condition plus project references; the generated client is one more package of that kind, and the `prisma/` workspace already owns the schema.
- **Alternatives:** (a) generate into `apps/api/src/platform/db/generated`: generated code inside application sources (eight tool configs need exclusions), the worker would import API sources, `prisma/tests` would reach into an app — rejected; (b) a new `packages/db` workspace: same mechanics, but brief 4.1 fixes the layout and `prisma/` already is the schema workspace — rejected; (c) a relative import across `rootDir`: TS6059/TS6307 and a `dist` path that does not exist at run time — rejected; (d) running TypeScript at run time or bundling: ADR-0002 section 3 — rejected; (e) passing the class in from `main.ts` (the developer's wiring): the same `rootDir` problem, and the worker would need its own composition (PR11-SEC-09). The developer's candidate (composite project exported as `@platform/prisma/client`) is adopted; its "boundaries carve-out for `platform/db/runtime.ts`" is not needed (D-ARCH-103).
- **Reversibility:** High (moving the client changes `generated.ts`, one `exports` entry and two tsconfig references).

### D-ARCH-103 · 2026-11-13 · principal-architect · D-TASK020-05: who may import `@platform/prisma/client`, as a value and as a type (ADR-0003 amendment 2026-11-13; data-model 7.2 amendment)
- **Decision:** (1) **No new pattern, no carve-out.** A bare workspace specifier that resolves to a repository file is classified by that file (`prisma/generated/**` = category `prisma-generated`), so the existing policies already decide it: verified that a service, another `platform/` folder and another package are refused ("only repositories import Prisma") and `platform/db` is allowed. The PR #32 reading that the rule "allows only repositories" is imprecise (`db-platform` is in `DATABASE_CODE`). A `module: { source }` selector matches nothing for a workspace specifier (verified), so the new policy selects by file category. (2) **Value or type.** After the `DATABASE_CODE` allow: disallow `{ to: prisma-generated, dependency: { kind: 'value' } }`, then allow it from `db-platform-core`, `prisma`, `tools-db` and `test`. Value import: the database platform core, `prisma/**`, `tools/db/**`, tests. Type-only import additionally: module and worker repositories and the two exact planned stores (`packages/audit/src/store/prisma-store.ts`, `apps/api/src/platform/outbox/writer.ts`). Everyone else: nothing. (3) **One value importer.** `apps/api/src/platform/db/generated.ts` joins `db-root-client` (pattern list with `client.ts`); it exports `PrismaClient`, the types `Prisma`, `AppTransactionClient = Prisma.TransactionClient`, `AppDb = TenantDb<AppTransactionClient>`, and a compile-time proof that every `SYSTEM_MODELS` name is a client delegate. `platform/db/index.ts` and `@platform/api/runtime` re-export the three types only, so `Prisma.sql`, `Prisma.raw` and `Prisma.Decimal` have no value path outside `platform/db`; this subsumes the data-model 7.5 rule "no `Prisma.Decimal` outside the FX repository" (the FX repository reads `Decimal` instances and writes strings; a needed constructor becomes a reviewed `platform/db` helper, not a lint relaxation). Verified: `platform/tx` importing `../db/generated.js` is refused; the services' type imports go through `../db/index.js`. (4) **Worker:** no composition of its own; runner from `createRuntimeServices`, types from the runtime entry; a direct type import adds the dependency and the project reference. (5) **`packages/audit`:** a structural port of the two tagged-template raw methods is preferred; a type-only import is allowed with the dependency and reference. (6) **Declarations:** exported repository and service functions are `async` or annotated (TS2883). (7) **CODEOWNERS** gains `/prisma/package.json` (the `exports` map decides what is importable), `/prisma/schema/_base.prisma` (the generator block decides the emitted shape) and `/apps/api/src/platform/db/generated.ts`.
- **Why:** The value path is where tenant isolation can be bypassed (a second client, `Prisma.raw`, `Prisma.sql` fragments), the type path is harmless; splitting them keeps repositories fully typed without handing them any constructor.
- **Alternatives:** the developer's "narrow carve-out for `platform/db/runtime.ts`" (rejected: not needed; `platform/db/**` is already allowed and a file-level carve-out would be a second list to maintain); allowing repositories value imports (rejected: contradicts ADR-0005 am. 10 item 2, repositories receive `TenantDb`); forcing every type through `platform/db` and forbidding direct type imports (rejected: `packages/audit` cannot import an app).
- **Reversibility:** High.

### D-ARCH-104 · 2026-11-13 · principal-architect · D-TASK020-05: runner activation shape (closes PR #11 R3-m1 (iii) and R3.6 once part 020-B merges)
- **Decision:** (1) `databaseRuntimeFromConfig(config, service, log)` takes no `Client`: it builds the client from `./generated.js` and returns a runtime whose `tenantTx` is defined; `createDatabaseRuntime` keeps its optional `Client` input as the unit-test seam. `RuntimeServices.tenantTx` becomes non-optional (`TenantTxRunner<AppTransactionClient>`); `assertPipelineReady` stays as defence in depth. One composition serves API and worker (PR11-SEC-09 "never a second composition"), so no `main.ts` change passes a class. (2) Consequences to test: with a runner the fresh-connection probe is real, so `database` readiness stays not ready until it passes and `startup()` makes a first pool query; suites that call `startup()` use fakes or Testcontainers. (3) Boot tests for both entry points; a Testcontainers integration test as `platform_app`: fresh-connection probe passes, a `transaction: 'tenant'` fixture route answers 200 through the composed `createApp`, a `DbError` surfaces as problem+json (PR11-SEC-09 items 3 and 4 at the tx slot). (4) PR #32 merges as it is: D-TASK020-05 stays "partial" until part 020-B merges (merge order PR #20, PR #32 unchanged, D-ORCH-044).
- **Why:** Injecting the class would keep `main.ts` and the worker each knowing about the client; importing it inside `platform/db` keeps the choke point single and makes the worker's runner identical by construction.
- **Alternatives:** inject from `main.ts` and `worker/main.ts` (rejected, see D-ARCH-102 (e)); fold the work into PR #32 (rejected: PR #32 is in review round 1 with a large surface, and the change edits `package.json`, `tools/tsconfig.json`, CODEOWNERS and `eslint.config.mjs`, each owned-path files that need their own security record scope).
- **Reversibility:** High.

### D-ARCH-106 · 2026-11-13 · principal-architect · PR32-SEC-01 (MEDIUM, security condition C1) / PR #32 code review m4 / threat model T-83: no external I/O inside a tenant transaction; three sanctioned homes; route phases `load` / `call` / `afterCommit`; the T-83 lint scope and the escape hatch (ADR-0005 amendment 11 items 17-21; ADR-0003 amendment 2026-11-13)
- **Decision:** (1) **Rule (ADR-0005 item 17):** a tenant transaction, in the API and in the worker, holds database statements and bounded in-memory work only; HTTP, queue, Valkey, object storage, SMTP and sleeps never run inside it. (2) **Sanctioned homes, in order of preference (item 18):** (a) the **outbox** (`outbox.publish(db, event)` in the handler transaction; the relay and the worker perform the effect) for everything asynchronous or durable, with `202` and a pollable resource; (b) a **`call` phase** when the response needs the external result (Stripe client secret, address suggestions, service points, pickup availability, integrity check); (c) an **`afterCommit` phase** for best-effort in-process continuation (the rate-shopping fan-out start). (3) **The proposed database-less `prepare(ctx)` pre-transaction phase is rejected (item 19):** every synchronous external call in M1 needs a tenant-scoped read first (the addressed shipment, order or payment must resolve under RLS to 404 before any carrier or gateway call, otherwise a foreign id spends carrier quota and leaks existence; amounts come from stored snapshots; the attempt counter is in the database), so such a phase would serve only CPU work. (4) **Phase model (ADR-0003 amendment):** `load(ctx)` runs in one short **read-only** tenant transaction (a write fails with 25006) and returns plain data; `call(ctx, loaded)` runs with **no transaction and no database handle**, gets an `AbortSignal` and must derive every external idempotency key from `loaded`, never from a random value; `handler(ctx, { loaded, called })` is today's field and the **only write transaction**, with the audit hook, outbox writes and a re-validation of what `load` read; `afterCommit(ctx, result)` runs after `COMMIT` and after the response, logs `api.after_commit_failed` on a throw and never changes the response, and is drained at shutdown. `transaction: none` allows only `handler` and `afterCommit`; `load` without `call` is refused; the D-ARCH-086 admission permit is taken per transaction and not held across `call`; the idempotency window wraps all phases; a stream result (TASK-044) is completed after `COMMIT`. A route with only a `handler` behaves exactly as today. (5) **T-83 lint scope (item 20)**, roots: R1 `withTenantTx` callbacks; R2 the `handler` of the first argument of `defineRoute(` in every function form unless the literal has `transaction: 'none'` as a string literal (a non-literal value or a spread counts as `tenant`; `fixtureRoute` defaults to `none` and is a root only with `transaction: 'tenant'`); R3 `handler: name` resolved by scope analysis to a function declaration or `const` function in the same file; R4 the `load` property once it exists; R5 whole-file roots by option `txFiles` (default `apps/api/src/platform/audit/**`, `apps/api/src/platform/outbox/writer.ts`, `packages/audit/src/store/**`, non-test files); R6 any function in any file with a parameter whose type annotation names `TenantDb`, `AppDb` or `AppTransactionClient` (option `txHandleTypes`; type-name based, not name based, so a readiness check taking `db: DatabaseRuntime` or an adapter taking `ctx: CarrierContext` is not a root): R6 is what reaches the real layering (`handler: controller.cancel` with an injected controller cannot be resolved, but the service method `create(db: AppDb, …)` it ends in is checked in its own file). `call` and `afterCommit` are never roots. (6) **Hatch and ratchets (item 21):** the only hatch is `transaction: none` (public tenancy, `audit.action` NONE, PR32-SEC-05 (d)); the route-metadata test pins the set of `transaction: none` operationIds (today the health operations); a unit test fails on any `eslint-disable` directive naming the rule under `apps/*/src` or `packages/*/src`; **runtime twin:** the API test lanes run with `DB_TX_IDLE_IN_TRANSACTION_TIMEOUT_MS=1000` (existing key, minimum 1 000 ms; production keeps 15 000) so a Mock `latency` scenario driven through a route that holds a transaction across a carrier call in another file fails a test. (7) **PR #32 fix cycle implements exactly this part of the ruling (condition C1) and adds no descriptor field:** roots R1, R2, R3, R5 and R6 in `tools/eslint-rules/no-external-calls-in-tenant-tx.mjs` (R4 is a one-line addition when `load` exists) with the `eslint.config.mjs` entry (`txFiles`, `txHandleTypes`); negative fixtures under `tests/fixtures/lint/rules/no-external-calls-in-tenant-tx/` for an inline `defineRoute` handler with `fetch` plus a `setTimeout` sleep, a named same-file handler, `deps.queue.add()` in a handler, `handler() {}` method shorthand, a spread literal without `transaction: 'none'`, a function in `apps/api/src/platform/audit/`, a function `create(db: AppDb)` calling `fetch` and a service method with `db: TenantDb` calling `deps.queue.add()` (R6); positive controls for a `transaction: 'none'` handler, `outbox.publish(db, event)` in a handler, the `fixtureRoute` default and a function with `ctx: CarrierContext` calling `fetch`; the `tools/lint/negative-fixtures.test.ts` entries; the three ratchets of (6) except the runtime twin; the `defineRoute` refusal of `transaction: none` with an audited action (PR32-SEC-05 (d)). (8) **Part 020-C** (third PR of TASK-020, D-ARCH-108) implements (4), the R4 line, the runtime twin and the stream hook. (9) **Interim rule until 020-C merges:** no `transaction: 'tenant'` route with external I/O may merge; nothing in Wave 0 needs one (TASK-026 is database-only), so the interim is empty in practice. (10) **Consumers:** TASK-043 (the outbox is the sanctioned in-transaction call; positive fixture; the writer is an R5 file), TASK-044 (stream completed after commit), TASK-049/052 (hash and verify in `call`, recommended), TASK-075/085/113 (each adds the binding names of its port to `names` with one fixture), TASK-079 (the Mock `latency` scenario is the instrument of the runtime twin), TASK-083/091 (fan-out without an open transaction; `createQuote` starts it in `afterCommit`), TASK-170 (checkout is `load` -> `call` -> `handler`), TASK-239/245/250/272 (read-then-call routes).
- **Why:** The finding is right that the lint as built protects no planned call site (the only per-request `withTenantTx` is the tx slot, which receives the handler by reference), and right that a lint without a sanctioned alternative turns into disables at the first checkout handler. The database-only rule plus the outbox already cover most effects; the `call` phase exists for the few synchronous responses that need an external result, and it keeps the property the architecture sells (every state change and its audit entry in one transaction) because only `handler` writes. The audit design already runs fail-closed VIEW entries in their own short transaction after the result set is fixed (TASK-029 sheet), so a request with more than one short transaction is not new.
- **Alternatives:** (a) outbox only (rejected: `client_secret`, suggestions and service points are synchronous responses); (b) a handler that opens its own short transactions (`ctx.tx.run`) (rejected: audit completeness would depend on each handler remembering, the pipeline cannot know which transaction carries the audit entry); (c) database-less `prepare` (rejected, (3)); (d) lint plus review only (rejected: erodes, exactly as the finding warns); (e) the existing idle-in-transaction (15 s) and Prisma (10 s) timeouts as the only control (rejected as the sole control: five concurrent 10 s holds exhaust the 10-connection pool; kept as the dynamic twin with a lower test value); (f) folding the phases into PR #32 (rejected: round 1 is already CHANGES_REQUESTED with M1, m1-m8, C1-C3 and the PR #20 union pending, the phases need the runner of part 020-B to be tested against a real transaction, and the first consumer is in batch 1.3).
- **Reversibility:** High (additive descriptor fields; lint scope is configuration).

### D-ARCH-107 · 2026-11-13 · principal-architect · PR32-SEC-09 (INFO) / PR #32 code review m7 / PR32-SEC-02 (condition C2) and D-TASK020-03: route authentication is a closed set of credential kinds; dual-mode permission; credential gate then permission gate (ADR-0008 amendment 4; api/README §8, §15 row 12)
- **Decision:** (1) **Shape:** `RouteSpec.auth` is one kind (as today) or a set; kinds `anonymous | session | refresh-cookie | quote-token | signature` (`session` keeps its name and means the bearer access token; **`refresh-cookie` is new** because `refreshSession`, `logoutSession` and `getCsrfToken` are called with an expired or absent access token and a generic bearer authenticator would make refresh impossible); `defineRoute` normalises to a frozen array; the accepted sets are exactly `[anonymous]`, `[session]`, `[refresh-cookie]`, `[signature]`, `[anonymous, session]` (`createQuote`) and `[session, quote-token]` (`getQuote`, `streamQuoteResults`); the set is the operation's `security` list read one to one, so parity is set equality. Verified against `openapi.yaml` on 2026-11-13: the 133 operations are 29 `[anonymous]`, 95 `[session]`, 3 `[refresh-cookie]`, 3 `[signature]`, 1 `[anonymous, session]` and 2 `[session, quote-token]`, and the four binding rules report no violation on the contract. A companion credential on a session route (`X-Quote-Token` on `claimQuote`, `saveQuote`, `createShipment`) is a declared header, not an alternative. (2) **`permissionAuthenticated`** (the contract's `x-permission-authenticated`) is required exactly on the dual-mode routes (permission `public` and the set `[anonymous, session]` or `[session, quote-token]`), must be a catalogued permission that is neither `selfService` nor `signatureOnly`, and is refused elsewhere. (3) **Binding rules** in `packages/authz` (`findRouteBindingViolations`, one negative test each, 95 % target): `AUTH_SET` (unlisted combination), `PERMISSION_AUTH` (catalogued or `authenticated` permission needs `[session]`; signature-only needs `[signature]`; a signature route declares a signature-only permission or `public`, which is D-TASK020-03 unchanged), `DUAL_MODE`, `CSRF_COOKIE` (a non-`GET` `refresh-cookie` route needs `csrf: true`); they subsume m7's refusal of `auth: 'anonymous'` with a non-`public` permission. (4) **Principal:** `credential` (one of the kinds; the anonymous principal carries `anonymous`); `authenticated` keeps its meaning, a user actor, so `tenantContextOf` is unchanged: a `quote-token` principal is a guest (`authenticated: false`, no actor, `guestTokenHash`), a `signature` principal is a provider (`authenticated: false`, no actor, permissions limited to its signature-only permission) — code-review n3 and the principal-kind remark of PR32-SEC-02; `principalOf` treats an unknown `credential` as anonymous. (5) **Authn slot rules for the real authenticators (TASK-052/055/091/171/261):** a present bearer must be valid and is never replaced by another alternative (401); with both a bearer and `X-Quote-Token` the bearer decides; no usable credential gives the anonymous principal if `anonymous` is in the set, else 404 `NOT_FOUND` if `quote-token` is in the set (A-078), else 401; a well-formed `X-Quote-Token` gives the guest principal (lowercase hex SHA-256), its verification being RLS and the quote lookup; `Cache-Control: private, no-store` when `anonymous` is not in the set and on any request that presented a credential, errors included. The PR #32 **stub** keeps failing closed: the anonymous principal when `anonymous` is in the set and no `Authorization` header, refresh cookie or `X-Quote-Token` is present, 401 with `private, no-store` otherwise. (6) **Authz (condition C2):** the **credential gate** runs for every permission value, `public` included (`route.auth` must contain `principal.credential`, else 401 `AUTH_REQUIRED`), then the **permission gate** (`public` passes except that a `session` principal on a route with `permissionAuthenticated` must hold it, 403 `AUTHZ_DENIED`; `authenticated` needs the user actor; a catalogued permission must be held). This is stricter and more exact than the review's wording `principal.authenticated`, which would reject every guest and signature route. (7) **PR #32 fix cycle implements all of it except the real authenticators:** `packages/authz/src/routes.ts` (kinds, `ROUTE_AUTH_SETS`, `BoundRoute.auth` as a readonly array plus `permissionAuthenticated` and `csrf`, the four rules and the adapted `SIGNATURE_AUTH`, `routes.test.ts`); `define-route.ts` (scalar sugar so existing fixtures and tests do not change, normalisation, `permissionAuthenticated`); `route-state.ts` and `define-route.ts` `Principal.credential`; `authn/authenticate.ts` stub; `authz/authorise.ts` (credential gate then permission gate) with tests: the leaky-authn seam (authn calls `next()` without a principal) on `public` + `signature`, `public` + `refresh-cookie`, `[session, quote-token]` and `[session]`, a principal whose credential is outside the set, and both branches of a dual-mode route (anonymous 200; session without the permission 403, with it 200); `tests/generated/route-metadata.ts` (`contractAuth` returns the set, set equality, `x-permission-authenticated` equality, `transaction: none` pin; seeded defects: a dropped `quote-token`, a refresh route declared `session`, a missing `permissionAuthenticated`, one on a non-dual route, an unlisted combination); the SEC-TC-29 helper predicate (PR32-SEC-06 (a): `private, no-store` when the operation's `security` has no empty alternative or the request carried a credential). (8) **Later owners:** TASK-052 bearer (`credential: session`, user actor from the verified `sub`; serves every route whose set contains `session`, never `refresh-cookie` routes); TASK-055 cookie authenticator and `csrf`; TASK-091 guest-token authenticator and `createQuote` branching on `principal.credential`; TASK-171/261 signature authenticators (D-TASK020-03 compensating controls (ii) of the security record); TASK-027 matrix rows per accepted credential kind and both dual-mode branches plus a credential outside the set; TASK-040 idempotency scope keyed by `principal.credential` (organisation, guest-token hash, or IP /64).
- **Why:** The shape must exist before the matrix generator (batch 0.8) and the first authenticator are written: today `contractAuth` folds `{} | bearerAuth` to `anonymous` (the authn slot would never read a present bearer, README §8) and `bearerAuth | quoteToken` to `quote-token` (parity cannot see a dropped alternative), `x-permission-authenticated` is in neither metadata nor parity so the matrix cannot test the tenant branch, and `session` conflates the access token with the refresh cookie. The set form mirrors the contract one to one; keeping scalar sugar makes the change mechanical. It also makes C2 implementable without a second pass over the same files.
- **Alternatives:** a structured `{ required, optional }` (rejected: cannot express "bearer or guest token" without a second field, and parity stops being set equality); array only (rejected: churn in every fixture for no gain); renaming `session` to `bearer` (rejected: churn; the name is documented); leaving it to TASK-052/091 (rejected: C2 needs the credential kind now, and a refresh route built on the bearer authenticator is wrong by construction); `[quote-token]` as a standalone set (rejected: no operation needs it; add by amendment when one does).
- **Reversibility:** High (metadata, rules and a stub; no contract change).

### D-TASK015-14..19 · 2026-11-13 · senior-developer · PR #33 fix cycle 1 (R1-M1..M3, R1-m1..m3, PR33-SEC-01..04)
- **Decision:** (14) The coverage gate's critical scopes follow TEST-STRATEGY §8 / D-QA-003: `apps/api/src/modules/payments/service`, `packages/shared/src/money` and `apps/api/src/modules/ledger` at 95/95, optional (inactive while absent or holding no measurable file, the scope folder itself being the source root), fail closed once source exists without a summary entry; `packages/ledger` is **kept**, justified as the literal path of AT-US-006-03 (EPIC-01 story), so a package of that name could never escape the gate; it costs one inactive case. (15) **Amends 04:** `openapi-breaking` runs after Semgrep and **before** the record step (a missing record, normal on the first push of an owned change, must not hide the contract result); with no release tag it runs a smoke comparison of the head contract with itself, so the container, the mount and the parser execute on every PR (R1-M1 Linux proof). Spec folder 0755, files 0644, mount unchanged otherwise. (16) **Amends 03:** the baseline is the highest strict-semver tag (`^v\d+\.\d+\.\d+(-[0-9A-Za-z.-]+)?$`, semver precedence computed in the script, not `--sort=-v:refname`) among tags merged into the base; records are Accepted ADRs (first status line) added or modified **tag..head** (a sanctioned break stays sanctioned until the next tag), naming each operation as a whole identifier; `--image` must equal the script's `OASDIFF_IMAGE`. (17) Pins: the two porcelain gates and openapi-breaking are held to one exact ASCII line with no step env, porcelain gates directly after the step they guard (`RequiredGate.after`); ci.yml workflow env `OASDIFF_IMAGE` must equal the script pin and no job may set it; a new repository-wide rule `gate-env` refuses `GATE_*`/`GATES_*` keys in any `env:` (they come only from the base-ref gate-tooling steps through `$GITHUB_ENV`); every non-comment line of ci.yml must be ASCII (the YAML subset trims Unicode blanks GitHub keeps). This closes R1-m2's precondition on D-TASK015-08 (the three new pins are now no weaker than the evidence pin). (18) PR33-SEC-04 (INFO) is fixed here because the tool was being changed anyway (one `clean` helper for every PR-controlled output). (19) R1-m1 is closed with a heavy end-to-end test (stub Jest, kind `jest`, `coverage: true`) rather than `unit.required_cases`, because inactive scope case names change when a scope activates (`packages/pricing (inactive)` → `packages/pricing lines`); the stable `overall` names go into `required_cases` with the 015-B hook (PR33-SEC-06). **Amends 11:** the merged `test:coverage` + `coverage:gate` + `coverage:diff` hook is a named 015-B deliverable with the checkpoint above (R1-m4).
- **Why:** the three MAJORs sat in code that starts to matter at the first tag; the smoke run gives a durable, per-PR Linux proof instead of a one-off; the persistence fix keeps main green after a sanctioned break; the scope list now matches the accepted test strategy instead of a path no document plans.
- **Alternatives:** `--user "$(id -u):$(id -g)"` instead of modes (rejected: runs the container as the runner user, wider than needed); a `!cancelled()` condition on the step instead of moving it (rejected: required-gates pins the step unconditional, and a condition is one more thing to pin); dropping `packages/ledger` (rejected: AT-US-006-03 names it literally); `required_cases` for R1-m1 (deferred, see 19).
- **Reversibility:** High (CI tooling; the base-ref copies govern later PRs).

From now on: after a PR merges, the orchestrator clears that worktree's `node_modules`; agents create new worktrees only when needed and reuse finished ones' directories; disk free space is checked before dispatching heavy runs (threshold 20 GB). Docker image/volume pruning needs the user (Docker Desktop's VHDX does not shrink on its own).
- **Reversibility:** High (dependencies reinstallable).

New: 06 Token endpoint rejects the credentials, 07 FedEx token endpoint 403 cool-down (D-060), 08 UPS token endpoint 403 on account A (D-060), 09 Token requests are rate-limited per carrier, 10 Missing expires_in is never cached.
  - **US-137** (`EPIC-06-carrier-integration.md`): map 7 → 8. New: 08 Not yet diffed by a person is allowed but reported (D-ARCH-057 item 1.4). Map 06 Live suite skipped and 07 Live sandbox runs (`@live-sandbox`) return to their map positions.

  (3) The one wording touch: in US-129 "Token never logged" the step "all logs of the scenarios above are scanned" became "all logs of all scenarios in this feature are scanned", because the scenario is now fifth, not last, and "above" would have pointed at four scenarios only; the assertion (no token value in any log of the feature's scenarios) is unchanged. (4) Verified by listing each block's scenario titles in order against the map rows: the first N titles match the map rows N = 8, 6, 5, 7, 8 (US-066, US-121, US-129, US-137, US-222). Note for qa-lead: all existing tests (`roles.test.ts`, `authorise.test.ts`, `matrix-doc.test.ts`, `generate.test.ts`, `authz-seed.int.test.ts`) already follow the map numbering (04 customer/partner, 05 Viewer outline, 06 Viewer denied, 07 partner roles, 08 Permission path); with the story order restored the single mixed-numbering defect in D-ORCH-049 (2) disappears without touching a test, so nothing is renumbered. qa-lead classifies the 13 new scenarios (US-066 09-12, US-121 07, US-129 06-10, US-137 08, US-222 09-10) in `gherkin-suite-assignments.json`, regenerates the map with `npm run quality:gherkin-map` and empties `KNOWN_DRIFT`; `docs/04-plan/tasks/WAVE-0x.md` AT ranges (US-066 01-12, US-121 01-07, US-129 01-10, US-137 01-08, US-222 01-10) already match the new counts. (5) PRD → 1.10 (§11 row) as the version trail for a story-file edit. REQUIREMENTS.md (1.9), NFR.md (1.5) and `traceability.md` (1.6) untouched: no REQ text, ID, link, priority, milestone, DC tag or count changed (434 REQs, 91 NFRs, 293 stories, 134 DC).

Moving the newer scenarios is cheaper and safer than renumbering tests and map rows (renumbering would also silently re-point every committed `junit.xml` ID in `docs/05-quality/tests/runs/`). The cost is that related scenarios (for example the two Compliance Auditor scenarios) no longer sit beside the guard scenario; the scenario titles name the decision so the topic stays findable. Classified as a wording-free reorder: no AC meaning, priority, milestone or DC tag moves, so the demo-critical set (US-066 stays DC) is unchanged.
- **Alternatives:** Renumber the US-066 tests to the story order and regenerate the map (rejected: breaks append-only, rewrites committed evidence IDs, and the other four stories would drift again on the next insertion). Renumber the map rows only (rejected: same). Keep the drift and rely on `KNOWN_DRIFT` (rejected by the code review: one ID would stay ambiguous). Do not alter "above" (rejected: a false positional reference in a security-relevant log-scan scenario).
- **Reversibility:** High (five scenario blocks reordered in three story files; one PRD row; no ID, test or code change). Future insertion rule for story-writer and product-manager: append new scenarios at the end of the block.

### D-ARCH-109 · 2026-11-13 · principal-architect · PR32-SEC-16 (INFO) / PR #32 code review R2-m4 and the open `Authorization` question of the PR32-SEC-16 owner note: a route reads only the credential kinds it declares; the refresh cookie is a credential only on the three `refresh-cookie` routes; a foreign credential neither authenticates, fails nor marks a response; the authn stub and the shared predicate become route-aware (ADR-0006 amendment 17; ADR-0008 amendment 5 items 1-4 and 6; api/README §8; ARCHITECTURE §7.4; risks R-ARCH-30)
- **Decision:** (1) **What is reconciled.** D-ARCH-107 (5)'s stub clause and ADR-0008 am. 4 item 4 (e) ("any request that presented a credential") treated the presence of any credential, the `Path=/` refresh cookie included, as a credential on every route. ADR-0006 am. 1 says the cookie is "ignored everywhere else", and the first sentence of ADR-0008 am. 4 item 4 says "only the kinds the route declares are considered". The latter two are the rule; the stub clause and (e) are replaced. The defect is latent today (nothing issues the cookie before TASK-055), but every browser that ever signed in would get 401 from `createSession`, `registerUser`, `createQuote`, public tracking and reference reads once TASK-055 lands, and the same holds for an expired access token that the client attaches to every call. (2) **The rule (ADR-0008 am. 5 item 1).** The authn slot reads the headers of the kinds in `route.auth` and no others; a credential of another kind, valid or not, is not parsed, not verified, not counted, cannot authenticate, cannot fail the request, cannot choose the principal and does not change the response headers. Per set: `[anonymous]` ignores bearer, cookie and `X-Quote-Token` (an expired or malformed bearer included; this answers the owner note's question: "a present bearer must be valid" was written for the three sets that contain `session` and never applied to `[anonymous]`, `[refresh-cookie]` or `[signature]`); `[session]` reads and verifies the bearer and ignores the cookie (no bearer gives 401 `AUTH_REQUIRED`; the cookie is never a second way to present a session); `[refresh-cookie]` reads one cookie and ignores a bearer (an expired access token must not fail refresh, logout or csrf); `[signature]` reads only its signature header; `[anonymous, session]` verifies a present bearer (401, never downgraded to the guest branch) and otherwise is anonymous, ignoring cookie and `X-Quote-Token`; `[session, quote-token]` verifies a present bearer, else takes a well-formed token, else 404, ignoring the cookie. (3) **Security effect.** The cookie can authenticate only `getCsrfToken` (safe method) and the non-`GET` routes with `csrf: true` (rule `CSRF_COOKIE`), so a `Path=/`, `SameSite=Strict` cookie that rides on every request of the host has a three-route reach; a rotated or revoked token sent anywhere else causes no family revocation, no `TOKEN_REUSE_DETECTED`, no security event (ADR-0006 am. 17). Handlers never see the headers either way (`RouteContext` projects declared headers only, PR32-SEC-05 (c)). (4) **Cache marking follows the declared kinds (replaces am. 4 item 4 (e)).** `private, no-store` when the set has no `anonymous` member and on a request that presented a credential of a declared kind, errors included; a foreign credential does not mark. The generic test (any `Authorization`, either cookie or `X-Quote-Token`) stays for a problem raised before a route is known and for an error raised before the authn slot ran, where it costs nothing because problem documents are `no-store` anyway. Reason: the reference lists are `public, max-age=3600` with ETags (REQ-DATA-016) and every signed-in browser carries the cookie; marking on presence would switch HTTP caching off for every signed-in user and add no confidentiality, since the response cannot vary by a credential the route does not read. (5) **Stub and predicate (TASK-020 part 020-B follow-up).** `presentedKinds(headers)` in `@platform/shared`; the stub sets the anonymous principal when `anonymous` is in the set and no declared kind is present, else 401 `AUTH_REQUIRED` with `private, no-store` (still fail-closed: it verifies nothing); the problem handler, the SEC-TC-29 helper and the contract stubs use the declared test for a known operation and the generic one for the two generic cases. The comments that name the "pending ruling" in `credentials.ts` and `authenticate.ts` are replaced. (6) **ADR-0006 am. 17 also corrects two wordings:** the cookie is read by three routes, not two (am. 1 and the §Tokens sentence omitted `getCsrfToken`, which am. 2 and api/README §8 already had read it), and with both cookies on one request (Compose shares `localhost` across ports; production hosts are separate) the one whose app matches the request is read and the other ignored unevaluated, no match giving 401 without touching token state. (7) **Owners and due.** TASK-020 part 020-B (the follow-up line; due before TASK-027 merges and before TASK-052 starts; security record); TASK-027 (a row per route and per foreign credential kind: result and `Cache-Control` equal the no-credential request; named rows `[anonymous]` + cookie 200, `[anonymous]` + expired bearer 200, `[session]` + cookie only 401); TASK-052 (reads `Authorization` only where `session` is declared); TASK-055 (reads the cookies only on `refresh-cookie` routes, one cookie by app, two modules name them, side-effect-free off the three routes); TASK-091 (reads `X-Quote-Token` only where `quote-token` is declared). (8) **Wording owed outside my files (security-analyst, `threat-model.md`; not edited here):** R-06 and T-17 ("read only by refresh and logout" becomes "read only by the routes that declare `refresh-cookie`: refresh, logout and csrf, and by nothing else"); T-06 and the SEC-TC-29 row (marking follows declared credentials; a foreign credential neither marks nor refuses; public reference data keeps `public, max-age=3600`); the PR32-SEC-16 owner note said the cookie "still makes the response `private, no-store`", which this ruling does not adopt (reason in (4)), so the next PR #32 record should say "closed by D-ARCH-109"; consider one SEC-TC (the next free ID after 75) for "a stale refresh cookie and an expired bearer on `[anonymous]` routes are ignored, and a `[session]` route never accepts the cookie".
- **Why:** The finding is right that "present means refuse" is an availability defect with a built-in temptation: the first time login answers 401 to a browser with a stale cookie, someone weakens the credential gate that C2 just closed. The two sentences that disagree were both mine; the one that was right (declared kinds only) was already in the amendment, and the stub clause went further than it because a stub that verifies nothing cannot tell a stale credential from a current one. Making the rule explicit per set, with the three foreign kinds, also answers the question that PR32-SEC-16 raised about `Authorization` and removes the same trap from the bearer authenticator (TASK-052) and the guest-token authenticator (TASK-091) before they are written.
- **Alternatives:** (a) a narrower cookie `Path` (rejected: `__Host-` requires `Path=/`, threat model T-17; dropping the prefix loses the protection against cookie injection from sibling subdomains, ADR-0006 am. 1, to buy a restriction the server enforces anyway); (b) keep "present means refuse" and have clients avoid sending the cookie (rejected: the cookie is HttpOnly and the browser attaches it, the client cannot strip it); (c) the cookie still marks the response `private, no-store` (the PR32-SEC-16 owner note; rejected for (4): it disables caching of the reference lists for every signed-in browser and protects nothing, because the response does not depend on the cookie); (d) strip the `Cookie` header at the edge outside `/api/v1/auth/*` (an ALB cannot rewrite request headers; CloudFront at M5 can through a per-behaviour cookie policy: optional defence in depth for platform-architect, not required here, because only the cookie authenticator reads the header and handlers never see it); (e) a request middleware that deletes the header on other routes (a mutation of the request for no gain over not reading it); (f) fix only the stub and leave the rule to TASK-052/055 (rejected: the shared predicate, the SEC-TC-29 helper and the TASK-027 rows depend on the rule before those tasks start).
- **Reversibility:** High (a rule, a stub and a predicate; no contract change, no cookie attribute change).

### D-ARCH-110 · 2026-11-13 · principal-architect · PR32-SEC-14 (INFO): a signature-only permission is satisfied by the signature principal; the gate changes, the provider principal stays `authenticated: false` (ADR-0008 amendment 5 item 5)
- **Decision:** (1) The finding is right: `authorise` requires `principal.authenticated` for every catalogued permission, while ADR-0008 am. 4 items 3 and 5 (b) define the provider principal as `credential: 'signature'`, `authenticated: false`, no actor, permissions limited to the route's own signature-only permission, and say it can satisfy exactly that permission. The text was right and the code was not: a `[signature]` route holding `webhook:stripe:receive` answers 401 to every valid webhook. (2) **Gate:** for a catalogued permission, if the catalogue marks it `signatureOnly` the principal's credential must be `signature` (the credential gate has already required membership of `route.auth`, and `PERMISSION_AUTH` binds a signature-only permission to `[signature]`) and the principal must hold the permission, else 403 `AUTHZ_DENIED`; no actor is required. Every other catalogued permission keeps the user-actor requirement (401) and then the held check (403). (3) **Principal:** unchanged. `authenticated: true` is never set for a provider and no actor is invented, because that would break the context builder's rule "authenticated if and only if an actor is present" (PR26-SEC-04) and attribute webhook writes to a user who does not exist. The signature authenticators build the principal only after the signature over the raw body verified, and the permission is never read from a header or a body. (4) **Owners:** the gate change is in the TASK-020 part 020-B follow-up (D-ARCH-109 (5); a TASK-020 file, and TASK-027 generates its rows at batch 0.8); TASK-171 and TASK-261 build the principals and test through the real `authorise` (valid 200, invalid 401, bearer on the route 401, principal without the permission 403); TASK-027 adds the two signature rows per `[signature]` route.
- **Why:** The matrix generator (TASK-027) and the webhook tasks (batch 6.2) would otherwise meet a gate that cannot pass a valid webhook, and the hurried fix is the one the owner note warns about: make the provider authenticated.
- **Alternatives:** make the provider principal `authenticated: true` with a synthetic actor (rejected, (3)); a second permission gate for signature routes (rejected: the rule is one branch on a catalogue flag that already exists); leave it to TASK-171 (rejected: the gate is a TASK-020 file and TASK-027's rows need it first).
- **Reversibility:** High.

### D-ARCH-111 · 2026-11-13 · principal-architect · PR32-SEC-12 (LOW) / PR #32 code review R2-m3: the T-83 lint's residual lexical shapes, what it reports when it cannot resolve a handler, and what stays out of reach (ADR-0005 amendment 11 item 22; TASK-020 part 020-C)
- **Decision:** (1) **Fail closed on what cannot be resolved in the file, but not on the sanctioned layering.** The review's remediation ("report a handler that is neither a function, a same-file function name nor a member expression") would also report an imported handler, which D-ARCH-106 (5) and the security record (item (h)) accept because R6 reaches the service in its own file. The ruling: report a `defineRoute`/`fixtureRoute` first argument that is not an object literal or a same-file `const` literal; walk a call handler through its function arguments (`timed(async () => ...)`); report a handler that is a function parameter, a `let`/`var` binding or a call with no function argument (so a route-building helper is reported at its `defineRoute` call); do **not** report a member expression (`controller.cancel`) or an imported binding. (2) The other shapes: aliased factories through import aliases; `names` matched on any receiver chain ending in the name plus one same-function `const` alias; methods of a class whose constructor has a `txHandleTypes` parameter property are roots; `scheduler.wait` and `Atomics.wait` are sleeps (`setTimeout` from `node:timers/promises` already was); a literal `import()` of an external module inside a root is external I/O; `createRequire` resolved through import aliases and namespace members; core `no-eval` on for `apps/*/src` and `packages/*/src`. One negative fixture per form. (3) **Limits written into the rule header and ADR-0005 am. 11 item 22:** a root calling an imported function that takes no handle and performs I/O, dynamic dispatch (`obj[name]()`) and handlers produced by a build step stay review items, answered by R6 at the service, the `names` option for ports and the runtime twin (D-ARCH-106 (6)). A false positive on an in-memory variable named like a port is fixed by renaming; there is no disable (the ratchet of D-ARCH-106 (6) stands). (4) **Owner and due:** TASK-020 part 020-C (D-ARCH-108: before batch 1.3, hard stop before TASK-044); the interim rule of D-ARCH-106 (9) (no tenant route with external I/O may merge) covers the gap and costs nothing today.
- **Why:** Wrapping handlers in a helper is the first refactor a module with ten routes will make; the rule must either follow it or refuse it, and refusing it is cheap because the sanctioned shapes (inline, same-file const, injected controller) all stay legal. The member-expression and import exemptions are not a loophole, they are the architecture: the lint is lexical and per file by design, and R6 plus the runtime twin cover the cross-file case.
- **Alternatives:** report every non-resolvable handler including member expressions and imports (rejected: it rejects the layered design of ADR-0003 and would be disabled within a week); a `routeFactories` allow-list for sanctioned helpers (deferred: nobody needs one yet, and adding one later is a lint-config line in a code-owned file); whole-program call-graph analysis (rejected: a different tool, and the runtime twin already catches the case at test time).
- **Reversibility:** High (lint scope is configuration; fixtures pin it).
